parts.title: Incomplete Sentences
parts.instructions: A word or phrase is missing in each of the sentences below. Four answer choices are given. Select the best answer to complete the sentence.

questions.text: The board has approved the ______ of two additional distribution centres in the eastern region.
questions.explanation: Between “the” and “of” a noun is required: “the construction of”.

questions.text: By the time the auditors arrive next Monday, the finance team ______ all supporting documents.
questions.explanation: “By the time” with a future reference (“next Monday”) calls for the future perfect: the work will be complete before the auditors arrive.

questions.text: Mr. Halloran has worked at Brightline Logistics ______ more than fifteen years.
questions.explanation: “for” introduces a duration (fifteen years); “since” would introduce a starting point, as in “since 2011”.

questions.text: The revised safety guidelines ______ to all warehouse personnel last Thursday.
questions.explanation: The guidelines are distributed, they do not distribute: past passive, consistent with “last Thursday”.

questions.text: Sales in the northern territory grew ______ after the advertising campaign was launched.
questions.explanation: The word modifies the verb “grew”, so an adverb is needed.

questions.text: ______ the renovation took longer than planned, the restaurant reopened on schedule.
questions.explanation: The two clauses contrast — the work overran, yet the restaurant reopened on time — which calls for the concessive “Although”.

questions.text: We are looking for a supplier ______ delivery times are consistently under three days.
questions.explanation: The delivery times belong to the supplier, so the possessive relative “whose” is required.

questions.text: Employees should log out of the system before ______ the building.
questions.explanation: Here “before” acts as a preposition, so the verb that follows takes the -ing form.

questions.text: The list of approved contractors ______ updated at the end of every quarter.
questions.explanation: The subject is “the list”, which is singular; “of approved contractors” is only a modifier. A classic agreement trap.

questions.text: The revised layout makes the assembly line considerably ______ than the previous one.
questions.explanation: “than” requires a comparative, and because “efficient” is a long adjective it forms one with “more”.

questions.text: Please ______ the attached invoice to your accounting department for processing.
questions.explanation: “forward something to someone” means to pass it on. “proceed” and “arrive” are intransitive, and “promote” does not carry that sense.

questions.text: The technicians completed the installation ______ without any assistance from the vendor.
questions.explanation: An emphatic reflexive pronoun: they did it themselves.

questions.text: Ms. Ibarra travelled to the Rotterdam plant ______ the new packaging equipment.
questions.explanation: Infinitive of purpose: she travelled in order to inspect the equipment.

questions.text: Applicants with ______ experience in freight forwarding will be given priority.
questions.explanation: “proven” is a past participle used as an adjective: demonstrated experience.

questions.text: If the shipment ______ delayed again, we will have to notify the client immediately.
questions.explanation: First conditional: present tense in the “if” clause, future in the main clause.

questions.text: ______ of the participants left before the closing remarks, so the room remained full until the end.
questions.explanation: “Few” goes with a plural countable noun and carries the negative sense that “so the room remained full” requires.

questions.text: The consultant's recommendations were both practical and ______.
questions.explanation: “both … and …” links two elements of the same kind, so after the adjective “practical” another adjective is needed.

questions.text: All of our offices will be closed ______ 25 December for the winter holiday.
questions.explanation: “on” is used before a specific date; “in” goes with months and years, “at” with clock times.

questions.text: Visitors ______ wear an identification badge at all times while on the factory floor.
questions.explanation: “at all times” signals an absolute obligation, so “must”. The other modals express mere possibility.

questions.text: Because of a scheduling ______, two departments reserved the same room for Tuesday afternoon.
questions.explanation: “scheduling conflict” is the set collocation for two bookings that overlap.

questions.text: Since ______ the sales team in 2019, Ms. Delacroix has doubled her regional revenue.
questions.explanation: “Since” followed by a verb with no expressed subject takes the -ing form.

questions.text: All expense claims ______ by a department manager before payment is issued.
questions.explanation: The claims are approved, they do not approve: passive after a modal, “must be + past participle”.

questions.text: The company installed additional lighting ______ the parking area would be safer at night.
questions.explanation: “so that” introduces a full clause with its own subject and verb; “in order to” would be followed by an infinitive.

questions.text: The programme is designed to ______ new hires with the company's safety procedures.
questions.explanation: After “to”, the bare infinitive is required: “familiarize someone with something”.

questions.text: The Hartwell Building, ______ was completed in 1998, will undergo a full renovation next spring.
questions.explanation: A non-defining relative clause between commas with an inanimate antecedent takes “which”; “that” cannot follow a comma.

questions.text: ______ of the two remaining candidates holds the required certification, so we will reopen the search.
questions.explanation: The sense is negative — the search is being reopened — and there are only two candidates, so “Neither”, agreeing in the singular with “holds”. “None” would imply at least three.

questions.text: Ridgeway Consulting has built a strong ______ for delivering projects ahead of schedule.
questions.explanation: “build a reputation for doing something” is the expected collocation.

questions.text: ______ in a plain envelope, the contract arrived without attracting any attention.
questions.explanation: The contract undergoes the action of being sent, so a past participle opens the sentence, equivalent to “Because it was sent…”.

questions.text: The manager praised the team for its careful ______ to detail throughout the audit.
questions.explanation: After the adjective “careful” a noun is needed, and “attention to detail” is itself a set phrase.

questions.text: Neither the supervisor nor the assistants ______ aware of the change in procedure.
questions.explanation: With “neither … nor …” the verb agrees with the second subject, here the plural “the assistants”. The past context rules out the present tense.

parts.title: Text Completion
parts.instructions: Read the texts that follow. A word, phrase, or sentence is missing in parts of each text. Select the best answer to complete the text.

passages.label: Questions 131-134 refer to the following e-mail.
passages.content:
To: All Staff
From: Yolanda Pratt, Finance Director
Date: 4 August
Subject: New expense system

Beginning on 1 September, all travel and entertainment expenses must be submitted through our new online portal, ClaimTrack. The paper forms currently in use will no longer be {{131}} after that date.

ClaimTrack allows you to photograph receipts with your phone and attach them directly to a claim. {{132}} Claims submitted with legible receipts are normally reimbursed within five working days.

Training sessions will be held in Room 2B during the last week of August. Attendance is not mandatory, but we strongly {{133}} it for anyone who submits claims regularly.

If you have questions, contact the finance help desk at extension 3300. Thank you for your {{134}} during the transition.

questions.explanation: Future passive: “will no longer be accepted” — the paper forms will stop being taken.

choices: This removes the need to keep printed copies for your records.
Paper receipts must still be mailed to the finance office.
The portal can be accessed only from computers inside the building.
Reimbursement rates have been revised for the coming year.
questions.explanation: The previous sentence explains that receipts are photographed, so the logical consequence is that no paper copies need keeping. Still mailing paper receipts, or restricting the portal to office computers, would contradict the paragraph.
The subject “we” needs a finite present-tense verb: “we strongly recommend it”.
After the possessive determiner “your”, a singular uncountable noun is needed: “your patience”.

passages.label: Questions 135-138 refer to the following letter.
passages.content:
Dear Ms. Okonjo,

Thank you for your order of 12 March for forty ergonomic desk chairs. Unfortunately, our supplier has informed us that the model you selected is {{135}} out of stock until early May.

We understand that this delay is inconvenient. {{136}} It is identical in design and carries the same five-year warranty, but it is available for immediate shipment.

If you would rather wait for your original selection, we will hold your order and {{137}} the delivery charge as a gesture of goodwill. Please let us know your decision by 25 March.

We {{138}} your understanding and value your continued business.

Sincerely,

Marcus Fenn
Customer Relations, Alderbrook Office Interiors

questions.explanation: The word modifies the adjectival phrase “out of stock”, so an adverb is needed.

choices: We are therefore able to offer an alternative model in the same price range.
Your payment has been refunded in full.
The chairs were unfortunately delivered to the wrong address.
Our showroom is open seven days a week.
questions.explanation: The next sentence opens with “It is identical in design”, so the pronoun requires that a replacement model has just been introduced.
“waive a charge” means to drop it — the only sense compatible with “as a gesture of goodwill”.
A present-tense closing formula: “We appreciate your understanding”.

passages.label: Questions 139-142 refer to the following memo.
passages.content:
MEMORANDUM

To: Marketing Department
From: Building Services
Re: Relocation to the fourth floor

Our department will move to the fourth floor over the weekend of 14-15 June. Packing crates will be delivered to your current work area on 12 June, and the movers will begin loading at six P.M. on Friday.

Please label every crate with your name and your new desk number. Crates that are not labelled {{139}} be placed in general storage, and retrieving them may take several days.

{{140}} Anything you no longer need should be placed in the recycling bins beside the service lift.

Personal electronics, keys and confidential files should be carried by hand rather than packed. The company cannot accept {{141}} for valuables left in crates.

Your network connection will be restored by Monday morning. If your telephone or computer is not working when you {{142}}, call the help desk at extension 5115.

questions.explanation: A certain future consequence of an instruction: “will be placed”. “would” would imply an unreal hypothesis.

choices: This is a good opportunity to reduce the volume of material you store.
The fourth floor has just been completely renovated.
The movers will pack your personal belongings for you.
The relocation has been postponed until July.
questions.explanation: The next sentence invites people to discard what they no longer need, so the paragraph must open on sorting. Having the movers pack for you contradicts the labelling instruction, and a July postponement contradicts the memo's own dates.
“accept responsibility for something”: after the verb, the singular uncountable noun is required.
After a future-referring “when”, English uses the present tense, never “will”.

passages.label: Questions 143-146 refer to the following notice.
passages.content:
PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT GRANTS — Applications now open

Northwind Industries will fund up to £1,200 per employee this year for external courses, conferences and professional certifications. Any member of staff who has completed at least twelve months of continuous service is {{143}} to apply.

Applications are reviewed twice a year, in April and October. Because the fund is limited, priority {{144}} to courses that relate directly to your current role or to a position you are actively preparing for.

{{145}} Applications submitted without one are returned unread.

Successful applicants are asked to share what they have learned with their team, either through a short presentation or a written summary. This requirement is taken {{146}}, and it is the main reason the programme has kept growing since 2019.

Forms are available on the intranet under Human Resources.

questions.explanation: After the verb “is”, a predicative adjective is needed: “is eligible to apply”.
“priority” undergoes the action, so the passive: “priority is given to”.

choices: Every application must include a written endorsement from your line manager.
The grant may also be used towards personal travel.
Applications are accepted at any time during the year.
The programme was suspended for the whole of last year.
questions.explanation: “Applications submitted without one” requires that a single mandatory item has just been mentioned — the manager's endorsement. Accepting applications year-round would contradict the April and October rounds.
“take something seriously”: the adverb modifies the verb, in the passive as much as the active.

parts.title: Reading Comprehension
parts.instructions: In this part you will read a selection of texts. Each text or set of texts is followed by several questions. Select the best answer for each question.

passages.label: Questions 147-148 refer to the following notice.
passages.content:
HILLCREST COMMUNITY POOL — Summer schedule change

From 1 July to 31 August, the pool will open at 6:00 A.M. on weekdays instead of 7:00 A.M. The additional hour is reserved for lane swimming only; recreational swimming begins at 8:00 A.M. as usual.

Weekend hours are unchanged: 8:00 A.M. to 8:00 P.M.

Members who wish to use the early hour must reserve a lane through the Hillcrest app no more than two days in advance. Walk-in access during that hour cannot be guaranteed.

Questions may be directed to the front desk or to schedule@hillcrestpool.example.

questions.text: What is the purpose of the notice?
choices: To advertise a new membership plan
To announce earlier weekday opening hours
To introduce a new swimming instructor
questions.explanation: “the pool will open at 6:00 A.M. on weekdays instead of 7:00 A.M.”: the point of the notice is the earlier weekday opening.

questions.text: What is indicated about the early morning hour?
questions.explanation: “must reserve a lane through the Hillcrest app”. The notice mentions neither an extra fee nor access for non-members.

passages.label: Questions 149-150 refer to the following text-message chain.
passages.content:
Dara Whitfield (10:42 A.M.)
The projector in the Aspen Room won't turn on. I have twelve clients arriving at eleven.

Owen Baptiste (10:44 A.M.)
Try the second remote, in the drawer under the table. The first one has been dead for a week.

Dara Whitfield (10:47 A.M.)
Found it — still nothing. The green light on the unit isn't on either.

Owen Baptiste (10:48 A.M.)
Then it's the power strip, not the projector. Move to the Birch Room, it's free until two. I'll bring the spare laptop cable up.

Dara Whitfield (10:49 A.M.)
You're a lifesaver. Could you also let reception know, so they redirect people?

Owen Baptiste (10:50 A.M.)
Already texting them.

questions.text: Why does Ms. Whitfield contact Mr. Baptiste?
choices: To report a piece of equipment that is not working
questions.explanation: Her first message reports that the projector will not turn on. Moving rooms comes later, and at Mr. Baptiste's suggestion.

questions.text: At 10:49 A.M., what does Ms. Whitfield most likely mean when she writes, "You're a lifesaver"?
choices: She is grateful for a workable solution.
She wants Mr. Baptiste to attend the meeting.
She is surprised that the projector now works.
She thinks reception has made a mistake.
questions.explanation: She is responding to a concrete fix — change rooms, bring a cable — so the phrase expresses gratitude.

passages.label: Questions 151-153 refer to the following advertisement.
passages.content:
KETTLE & KIN — Now hiring, all locations

Kettle & Kin operates eleven neighbourhood cafés across the metropolitan area. We are currently recruiting for the following positions:

Baristas (full and part time) — no experience necessary; paid four-week training provided
Shift Leaders — minimum one year of food-service supervision required
Bakers — 4:00 A.M. start; previous production baking experience essential

All employees receive one free meal per shift, a 40% discount on retail items, and transit reimbursement of up to £70 per month. Full-time staff join our health plan after ninety days.

We promote from within: nine of our eleven current store managers began as baristas.

Apply in person at any location with a printed résumé, or online at kettleandkin.example/jobs. Interviews are held on Tuesdays and Thursdays.

questions.text: What is stated about the barista position?
choices: It requires a year of previous experience.
It is available part time only.
It begins early in the morning.
questions.explanation: “no experience necessary; paid four-week training provided”. The 4 A.M. start applies to bakers and the year of experience to shift leaders.

questions.text: What benefit is available to every employee?
questions.explanation: “All employees receive […] transit reimbursement of up to £70 per month”. The health plan is limited to full-time staff after ninety days.

questions.text: Why does the advertisement mention the store managers?
choices: To explain a recent change in management
To identify who conducts the interviews
questions.explanation: “We promote from within” comes immediately before the statistic, so it serves to illustrate prospects for advancement.

passages.label: Questions 154-156 refer to the following e-mail.
passages.content:
To: Priya Raman <p.raman@vellmarkdesign.example>
From: Colin Aduba <c.aduba@northgatelibrary.example>
Date: 8 October
Subject: Signage project — revised scope

Dear Ms. Raman,

Thank you for the proposal you submitted last week for the interior signage at our Northgate branch. The design committee reviewed it on Monday and was impressed by the wayfinding concept, particularly the colour coding by floor.

We do need to revise the scope before we can approve a contract. The renovation of the third floor has been deferred to next year, so signage for that floor should come out of the current phase. That reduces the number of panels from fifty-eight to forty-one.

We would also like to add six free-standing directory units for the ground-floor lobby, which were not in the original brief.

Could you send a revised quotation covering both changes by 18 October? Our board meets on 22 October and I would like to bring a final figure to that meeting.

One further note: the library will remain open throughout installation, so any work in public areas must take place after 6:00 P.M.

Best regards,

Colin Aduba
Facilities Manager, Northgate Library

questions.text: What is the main purpose of the e-mail?
choices: To request an updated price quotation
To ask for additional design samples
questions.explanation: The central request is “Could you send a revised quotation covering both changes by 18 October?”. The original proposal is in fact well received.

questions.text: What is indicated about the third floor?
choices: Its signage will be installed first.
It will be permanently closed to the public.
It needs more panels than expected.
questions.explanation: “The renovation of the third floor has been deferred to next year” — hence its signage leaving the current phase.

questions.text: What restriction does Mr. Aduba mention?
choices: Work in public areas must be done in the evening.
Only library staff may handle the panels.
The budget cannot exceed the original figure.
Installation must be completed before 22 October.
questions.explanation: “any work in public areas must take place after 6:00 P.M.”. 22 October is the board meeting, not an installation deadline.

passages.label: Questions 157-159 refer to the following article.
passages.content:
MARITIME QUARTER GETS A SECOND LIFE

PORTHAVEN (14 May) — For thirty years the warehouses along Dock Road stood empty, too solid to fall down and too awkward to convert. This month the first of them reopened as the Porthaven Makers' Yard, a shared workshop for eighty small manufacturers.

The conversion was funded by a mix of city grants and rent paid in advance by future tenants — an unusual arrangement that the project's director, Ines Cardozo, says was the only way to begin. [1] "Banks wanted a finished building before they would lend, and we needed money before we could finish one," she said. [2]

Tenants pay between £180 and £600 a month depending on floor area, well below the £1,100 average for comparable industrial space in the city. [3] In exchange, they commit to a three-year lease and to opening their workshops to the public one Saturday a month.

[4] Two further warehouses are scheduled for conversion, the second of them due to open in eighteen months. Ms. Cardozo expects demand to keep outrunning supply: the Makers' Yard received more than four hundred applications for its eighty units.

questions.text: What is the article mainly about?
choices: The reopening of a converted warehouse
A dispute between a city and its lenders
questions.explanation: The subject is the opening of the Porthaven Makers' Yard inside a converted warehouse.

questions.text: What does Ms. Cardozo suggest about conventional bank financing?
choices: It was not available when the project began.
It required a longer lease term.
It was arranged by the city.
questions.explanation: Her quotation describes a deadlock: banks wanted a finished building, but money was needed to finish one. Hence the grants-plus-advance-rent arrangement.

questions.text:
In which of the positions marked [1], [2], [3] and [4] does the following sentence best belong?
"The saving comes with an obligation."
questions.explanation: The sentence bridges the low rents mentioned before [3] and the obligation introduced by “In exchange” immediately after.

passages.label: Questions 160-162 refer to the following online chat discussion.
passages.content:
Rosalind Achebe (2:03 P.M.)
Has anyone heard back from Tamsin about the Q3 figures? I need them for the deck by Thursday.

Peter Lindqvist (2:05 P.M.)
She's out until Wednesday. Her out-of-office message says to contact Devi for anything urgent.

Devi Sharma (2:06 P.M.)
I have the raw numbers but not the commentary. I can send you a spreadsheet this afternoon if that helps.

Rosalind Achebe (2:07 P.M.)
The numbers are what I need — I'll write the commentary myself. Are the returns figures final?

Devi Sharma (2:09 P.M.)
Everything except September returns. Those close on Friday, so the total could still move by half a percent.

Peter Lindqvist (2:10 P.M.)
Then mark that slide "provisional". Ravi got asked about a similar number in July and it was awkward.

Rosalind Achebe (2:11 P.M.)
Good call. Devi, send whatever you have and I'll flag the returns line.

questions.text: Why did Ms. Achebe start the discussion?
choices: To obtain data she needs for a presentation
To report an error in a spreadsheet
To ask why a colleague is absent
questions.explanation: “I need them for the deck by Thursday”: she is after the third-quarter figures for her presentation.

questions.text: What is suggested about the September returns figures?
choices: They will not be included at all.
questions.explanation: “Those close on Friday, so the total could still move by half a percent.”

questions.text: At 2:10 P.M., what does Mr. Lindqvist imply?
choices: Ravi should prepare the slide instead.
The July figures turned out to be incorrect.
Presenting an unlabelled estimate has caused a problem before.
questions.explanation: He recommends the “provisional” label by citing an awkward precedent: the problem came from the missing caveat, not from the figure itself.

passages.label: Questions 163-165 refer to the following letter.
passages.content:
Ferrand & Hoyle Chartered Surveyors
14 Blackfriars Row, Leeds LS1 4QQ

2 November

Mr. Anselm Krige
Krige Timber Products
Unit 9, Calder Industrial Estate

Dear Mr. Krige,

Following my inspection of the roof structure at Unit 9 on 28 October, I am writing to summarise my findings ahead of the full report, which will reach you within ten working days.

The steel frame is in sound condition, and I found no evidence of the corrosion that concerned you. The staining on the north wall is the result of a blocked gutter rather than any failure of the roof covering itself. Clearing the gutter and renewing approximately four metres of flashing should resolve it. I would expect that work to cost between £900 and £1,400.

I must, however, draw your attention to a separate matter. The roof lights above the finishing bay are the original 1987 units and have become brittle. They are not a safety hazard at present, but I would not recommend deferring their replacement beyond the next two years.

My full report will include photographs, moisture readings and a schedule of recommended works with indicative costs.

Yours sincerely,

Bernadette Hoyle, MRICS

questions.text: Why did Ms. Hoyle write the letter?
choices: To request payment for a completed report
questions.explanation: “to summarise my findings ahead of the full report”: these are preliminary conclusions, the inspection having already taken place on 28 October.

questions.text: What did Ms. Hoyle determine about the staining on the wall?
choices: It indicates corrosion of the steel frame.
Its cause could not be identified.
It requires replacing the entire roof covering.
It was caused by a drainage problem.
questions.explanation: “the result of a blocked gutter rather than any failure of the roof covering”: a blocked gutter, so a drainage problem.

questions.text: What does Ms. Hoyle recommend concerning the roof lights?
choices: Repairing them before the end of the month
Leaving them exactly as they are
questions.explanation: “I would not recommend deferring their replacement beyond the next two years”: no safety emergency, but replacement inside two years.

passages.label: Questions 166-169 refer to the following online review.
passages.content:
www.tovarahotels.example/harbourside/reviews

TOVARA HARBOURSIDE — Guest reviews (page 1 of 46)

★★★★☆  "Right for a working trip, less so for a holiday"
Reviewed by G. Almeida — stayed three nights in February

I booked the Harbourside for a conference at the centre next door, and for that purpose it is hard to beat. The walk takes four minutes, the business centre is open around the clock, and the front desk had my printing waiting for me when I came down at 6:30 A.M.

The room itself was quiet and generously sized, with a desk you can actually work at rather than the narrow shelf most hotels install. Housekeeping never once moved my papers, which I appreciated more than I expected to.

Two reservations. First, the restaurant closes at nine, which is early for a hotel of this size; on my second evening I ended up eating a sandwich from the lobby shop. Second, the much-advertised harbour view applies to roughly a third of the rooms — mine faced the car park, and nobody mentioned that when I booked.

I would return for work without hesitation. If I were bringing my family, I would look at the Tovara Bayside instead, which I gather has a pool.

Was this review helpful?  [Yes 214]  [No 11]

questions.text: What is indicated about the hotel's location?
choices: It is next to a conference venue.
It is far from the city centre.
It is beside a railway station.
questions.explanation: “a conference at the centre next door […] The walk takes four minutes.”

questions.text: What did Mr. Almeida particularly appreciate about his room?
choices: The quality of the work space
questions.explanation: He singles out “a desk you can actually work at”, and that housekeeping never moved his papers. The view is a complaint, not a compliment.

questions.text: What complaint does Mr. Almeida make about the restaurant?
questions.explanation: “the restaurant closes at nine, which is early for a hotel of this size”.

questions.text: What does Mr. Almeida suggest about the Tovara Bayside?
choices: It costs less than the Harbourside.
It is closer to the conference centre.
questions.explanation: “If I were bringing my family, I would look at the Tovara Bayside instead, which I gather has a pool.”

passages.label: Questions 170-171 refer to the following memo.
passages.content:
MEMO

To: All laboratory staff
From: Yusuf Bello, Quality Manager
Date: 15 May
Subject: Calibration logs

Beginning Monday, calibration entries must be made in the electronic log at the moment of calibration, not at the end of the shift. Our auditor flagged fourteen entries last month that had been recorded up to nine hours after the reading was taken.

The tablets mounted at each bench are now configured for log entry, so there is no longer any reason to walk to the office terminal.

Paper logs will be collected on Friday and archived. Do not continue to use them in parallel: duplicate records were the second finding in the audit.

Bench leaders will review entries every Monday morning.

questions.text: What change is being introduced?
choices: The bench tablets will be removed.
Calibrations will be carried out twice a day.
A new auditor has been appointed.
Calibrations must be logged as they are performed.
questions.explanation: “entries must be made […] at the moment of calibration, not at the end of the shift”.

questions.text: What are staff instructed to stop doing?
choices: Using the office terminal for calibration data
Keeping paper records at the same time
questions.explanation: “Do not continue to use them in parallel”, referring to the paper logs, whose duplication was the audit's second finding.

passages.label: Questions 172-175 refer to the following information.
passages.content:
CALDERWOOD FILM FESTIVAL — Volunteer information

Thank you for volunteering. Please read this page carefully; it answers most of the questions we receive.

SHIFTS
Morning 8:00 A.M. – 1:00 P.M.  |  Afternoon 12:30 P.M. – 5:30 P.M.  |  Evening 5:00 P.M. – 10:30 P.M.
Shifts overlap by thirty minutes so that duties can be handed over in person. Do not leave your post until your replacement has arrived.

ROLES
Box office — ticket collection and same-day sales. The Friday training session is required.
Ushers — seating, accessibility assistance, screening-room checks. No training required.
Hospitality — the filmmakers' lounge. Volunteers must be eighteen or over.
Transport — collecting guests from the station. A valid driving licence and two years' driving experience are required.

WHAT WE PROVIDE
A festival pass valid for any screening on days you are not working, two meal vouchers per shift, and a volunteer jacket (returnable at the end of the festival).

WHAT WE ASK
Arrive fifteen minutes before your shift begins. Wear dark trousers or a dark skirt with the jacket. Photography inside the screening rooms is not permitted, even during your break.

CANCELLATIONS
Telephone the volunteer line on 0900 55 21 44. Please do not cancel by e-mail — that inbox is not monitored during festival week.

questions.text: What is stated about the shift times?
choices: They are identical for every role.
They may be exchanged with other volunteers.
questions.explanation: “Shifts overlap by thirty minutes so that duties can be handed over in person.”

questions.text: Which role requires attending a training session?
questions.explanation: “Box office — […] The Friday training session is required.” Ushers need no training at all.

questions.text: What do volunteers receive?
choices: A cash payment for each shift
questions.explanation: “two meal vouchers per shift”. Transport is for guests rather than volunteers, and no payment is mentioned.

questions.text: How should volunteers report that they are unable to work?
questions.explanation: “Telephone the volunteer line […] Please do not cancel by e-mail”.

passages.label: Questions 176-180 refer to the following advertisement and e-mail.
passages.content:
MERIDIAN WORKS — Flexible workspace in central Bristol

Hot Desk — £145/month — unreserved desk, 8 A.M. to 8 P.M. on weekdays
Resident Desk — £260/month — your own desk, 24-hour access
Studio (2-4 people) — £680/month — lockable room, 24-hour access

passages.label: Questions 181-185 refer to the following article and letter.
passages.content:
TRANSIT AUTHORITY TRIMS ROUTE 42

EASTVALE (2 November) — The Eastvale Transit Authority will shorten Route 42 from 14 December, ending the service at Fenwick Interchange rather than continuing to Marley Green. The authority says the final three stops carried an average of eleven passengers a day last year, against a network average of two hundred and forty.

Riders travelling beyond Fenwick will be able to transfer to the new Route 42B minibus, which will run hourly on weekdays and every ninety minutes on Saturdays. There will be no Sunday service.

Deputy director Hana Vogel said the change would let the authority add two morning departures on Route 42 itself, where crowding has been the subject of repeated complaints. "We are moving capacity to where the passengers are," she said.

The authority held two public meetings in September. Attendance was low — nineteen people in total — a fact critics attribute to the meetings' 2 P.M. start.

To the Editor,

Your report on Route 42 repeated the transit authority's figure of eleven passengers a day without asking how it was produced.

I have used the Marley Green stop for nine years. The count was taken in the first week of August, when the packing plant that employs most of us shuts for its annual holiday. In any other week the 7:10 service alone carries fifteen to twenty of us.

I do not dispute that the two extra morning departures are needed; the buses from Fenwick are genuinely overcrowded. But the replacement minibus runs hourly, and my shift starts at 6:45 A.M. An hourly service that does not begin until seven is not a replacement — it is a removal.

As for the public meetings, I would gently point out that a two o'clock meeting on a Tuesday is not accessible to people who work shifts. That is presumably why nineteen people came.

Constance Ebele
Marley Green

questions.text: What change to Route 42 was announced?
choices: It will be extended to Marley Green.
It will operate on weekdays only.
It will end at an earlier stop.
It will be replaced entirely by minibuses.
questions.explanation: “ending the service at Fenwick Interchange rather than continuing to Marley Green”: the terminus moves back up the line.

questions.text: According to the article, why is the authority making the change?
choices: To comply with a new regulation
To move capacity to busier parts of the route
questions.explanation: Ms. Vogel: “We are moving capacity to where the passengers are”, hence the two extra morning departures.

questions.text: What does Ms. Ebele suggest about the passenger count?
choices: It included transfers from other routes.
It was taken during an unrepresentative week.
questions.explanation: The count was taken in the first week of August, while the plant that employs most riders was shut for its annual holiday.

questions.text: What concern does Ms. Ebele raise about Route 42B?
choices: It will be more expensive than Route 42.
It does not stop at Fenwick Interchange.
It does not start early enough for her shift.
questions.explanation: Her shift starts at 6:45 A.M. whereas the hourly replacement service does not begin until seven.

questions.text: On what point do the article and the letter agree?
choices: The public meetings were well attended.
The extra morning departures on Route 42 are needed.
The packing plant should change its holiday dates.
questions.explanation: The article cites the morning crowding, and Ms. Ebele writes “I do not dispute that the two extra morning departures are needed”.

passages.label: Questions 191-195 refer to the following product page, review and response.
passages.content:
BRISTLECONE OUTDOOR — Tarn 2 tent

Weight: 1.9 kg packed
Sleeps: 2
Waterproof rating: 4,000 mm flysheet, 6,000 mm groundsheet
Poles: aluminium alloy, colour-coded
Price: £249

The Tarn 2 was designed for three-season use in exposed conditions. Its low profile and six guy points make it unusually stable in wind for a tent of this weight.

Two doors and two vestibules mean neither occupant has to climb over the other. The inner tent can be pitched on its own in dry conditions, or the flysheet used alone as a shelter.

Not recommended for winter mountaineering or for use below -5 °C.

Every Bristlecone tent carries a five-year guarantee against manufacturing defects. Damage from ordinary wear, accidents or misuse is not covered, but our Bristlecone Mend service will repair almost anything for a fixed fee of £40 plus parts.

Free delivery on orders over £100. Returns accepted within sixty days provided the tent has not been pitched outdoors.

★★★☆☆  "Excellent tent, one design flaw"
Reviewed by H. Okwuosa — verified purchase

Twenty-two nights in this tent across Snowdonia and the Cairngorms, including one night of sustained fifty-mile-an-hour wind on a col where I fully expected to be walking out at three in the morning. It did not move. The six guy points are not marketing.

The two doors are worth the extra two hundred grams over a single-door tent, and being able to pitch the inner on its own was genuinely useful in Spain last month.

My complaint is the zip on the left vestibule, which snagged on the storm flap from the second week and has now failed completely. Looking at the forum, I am not the first. Whether that counts as a manufacturing defect or as ordinary wear is presumably a matter of opinion, and I suspect I know which way it will go.

Would still buy it again.

Response from Bristlecone Outdoor — Customer Care

Thank you for this, and for the detail — a col in the Cairngorms in fifty-mile-an-hour wind is exactly what the Tarn 2 was designed for.

On the vestibule zip: you are right that this has come up before. We changed the storm-flap geometry on units manufactured after March this year for precisely that reason. Tents made before that date are covered by the guarantee for this specific fault, wear or not, and we are treating it as a manufacturing issue rather than sending it to Mend.

Please contact us with your order number and we will collect the tent and either repair or replace it at no cost to you. If you need it before your next trip, tell us the date and we will send a replacement out first.

We have also added a note to the product page.

— Ravi Kulkarni, Customer Care

questions.text: What does Mr. Okwuosa praise about the tent?
questions.explanation: “It did not move. The six guy points are not marketing”, after a night of fifty-mile-an-hour wind.

questions.text: What problem does Mr. Okwuosa describe?

It will be repaired free of charge.
It will be the first case of its kind.
It will be treated as ordinary wear.

The company will charge the fixed Mend fee.
The company will cover the repair under its guarantee.

meta.notes: Complete Reading section in the official shape: Part 5 (30), Part 6 (16, four texts), Part 7 (54: ten single passages, two double, three triple). Numbered 101-200, 75 minutes.

parts.title: Incomplete Sentences
parts.instructions: A word or phrase is missing in each of the sentences below. Four answer choices are given. Select the best answer to complete the sentence.

questions.text: Vessel arrivals at Terminal 4 are posted hourly so that hauliers can plan their collections more ______.
questions.explanation: “Plan” is a verb, so it takes an adverb: “plan their collections more accurately”.

questions.text: By the time the new sorting hub opens in March, the company ______ more than €4 million in automation.
questions.explanation: “By the time” plus a future event calls for the future perfect: the investing will be complete before the hub opens.

questions.text: All catering orders must be confirmed ______ writing at least seventy-two hours before the event.
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is “in writing”, meaning in a written document.

questions.text: The banquet hall can be arranged in several ______ depending on the size of the party.
questions.explanation: “Several” must be followed by a plural noun: “several configurations”.

questions.text: The publisher decided to ______ the launch of the biography until the author's tour dates were confirmed.
questions.explanation: “Postpone … until” is the only choice that means moving an event to a later date, which is what the unconfirmed tour dates require.

questions.text: Damaged pallets ______ from the container before the shipment was released to the customer.
questions.explanation: The pallets receive the action, so a past passive is needed to match “was released”.

questions.text: Guests staying more than five nights receive a ______ discount on all spa treatments.
questions.explanation: An adjective is needed before the noun “discount”: “a substantial discount”.

questions.text: The freight forwarder recommends ______ perishable goods at least a week before the holiday period.
questions.explanation: “Recommend” takes a gerund when no object follows it: “recommends booking”.

questions.text: ______ the ferry crossing was delayed by fog, the delegates arrived in time for the opening reception.
questions.explanation: The delay and the on-time arrival conflict, so a concessive conjunction is required. “Because” would make the delay the reason they were punctual.

questions.text: The hotel's night manager handled the double-booking with impressive ______.
questions.explanation: After the preposition “with” and the adjective “impressive”, a noun is required: “with impressive composure”.

questions.text: Ms. Adeyemi ______ the conference centre's audiovisual team since it was founded eight years ago.
questions.explanation: “Since” with a past starting point calls for the present perfect, showing that she still leads the team.

questions.text: The distribution centre ______ we visited last month processes 12,000 parcels an hour.
questions.explanation: “Visited” has no object, so the relative pronoun fills that gap. “Where” is tempting because the noun is a place, but it would leave “visited” incomplete.

questions.text: Please ensure that the invoice number is printed ______ on the outside of every carton.
questions.explanation: An adverb is needed to modify the verb “is printed”: “printed legibly”.

questions.text: The trade fair stand must be dismantled ______ midnight on Sunday.
questions.explanation: “By” marks a deadline for a single completed action; “until” would describe an activity continuing up to midnight.

questions.text: Bookshops that return unsold copies within ninety days are eligible for a full ______.
questions.explanation: Money returned for goods sent back is a refund; a “reduction” would lower a future price rather than repay one already paid.

questions.text: The catering manager praised the kitchen staff for their ______ under pressure.
questions.explanation: The praise is for a quality the staff showed, and “professionalism” is the noun naming it. “Profession” would mean their trade, not their conduct.

questions.text: The list of approved freight carriers ______ reviewed by the procurement committee each quarter.
questions.explanation: The subject is the singular “list”, not the plural “carriers” inside the prepositional phrase.

questions.text: When the courier arrived at the loading bay, the warehouse team ______ already sealed the last crate.
questions.explanation: The sealing happened before the past arrival, so the past perfect is required.

questions.text: Delegates found the keynote speaker's account of the industry's transformation deeply ______.
questions.explanation: The account produces the effect, so the present participle is used; “fascinated” would describe the delegates, not the account.

questions.text: The hotel group announced the ______ of three boutique properties on the Adriatic coast.
questions.explanation: Between “the” and “of” only a noun can stand: “the acquisition of”.

questions.text: ______ of the two banquet rooms has its own service entrance.
questions.explanation: The singular verb “has” and the singular “its” rule out “both”, which would take “have”. “Every” cannot be followed by “of”.

questions.text: The revised distribution agreement ______ by both parties before the end of the fiscal year.
questions.explanation: The agreement is what gets signed, and the agent appears in a “by” phrase, so the modal passive is required.

questions.text: Freight rates on the northern route have risen ______ since the canal restrictions were introduced.
questions.explanation: The blank describes how the rates have risen, which calls for an adverb.

questions.text: The events team arranged for a second shuttle bus ______ guests from the airport terminal.
questions.explanation: The pattern “arrange for + noun + to + verb” states the purpose of the arrangement.

questions.text: Visitors ______ wear a high-visibility vest at all times in the container yard; there are no exceptions.
questions.explanation: “There are no exceptions” signals an obligation rather than a permission or a possibility.

questions.text: The film critic's column appears ______ Thursdays in the weekend supplement.
questions.explanation: Days of the week take “on”, including recurring plural days: “on Thursdays”.

questions.text: The conference organisers apologised for the ______ caused by the change of venue.
questions.explanation: After “the” and before the reduced clause “caused by”, a noun is needed: “the inconvenience caused”.

questions.text: Next Monday the newsroom ______ to its refurbished offices on Kandinsky Street.
questions.explanation: “Next Monday” places the move in the future, which the three past forms cannot express.

questions.text: The banquet menu can be adapted for vegetarian guests, ______ the kitchen is notified at least a day in advance.
questions.explanation: The notice is a condition on the adaptation, and “provided that” states that condition. “Even if” would say the notice makes no difference.

questions.text: All complimentary breakfast vouchers must be ______ before 10:30 A.M.
questions.explanation: A voucher is “redeemed” when it is exchanged for what it entitles the holder to; the other verbs describe getting something back rather than using it.

parts.title: Text Completion
parts.instructions: Read the texts that follow. A word, phrase, or sentence is missing in parts of each text. Select the best answer to complete the text.

passages.label: Questions 131-134 refer to the following e-mail.
passages.content:
To: All Export Desk Staff
From: Bertil Lindqvist, Operations Manager
Date: 12 May
Subject: Customs paperwork from 1 June

From 1 June, every consignment leaving our Rotterdam depot must {{131}} by an electronic customs declaration lodged at least four hours before collection. The paper declaration will remain valid only for shipments booked before that date.

Lodging a declaration takes about ten minutes on the Trade Gateway portal. {{132}}, the system stores each exporter's details, so a repeat customer can be processed in a fraction of that time.

{{133}} Please raise them with your team leader rather than with the carrier, as the carrier is not party to the new arrangement.

Log-in details will be sent to your work address on 26 May. Drivers will not be permitted to leave the yard {{134}} a declaration reference is attached to the manifest.

questions.explanation: The consignment is the thing accompanied, and the agent follows in a “by” phrase, so the modal passive is needed: “must be accompanied by”.
Ten minutes sounds slow, and the stored details make repeat claims much faster, so the two sentences stand in contrast.

choices: The portal was tested at three other depots this spring.
You may find that some customers have questions about the new procedure.
Customs officers will visit the depot during the first week of June.
The four-hour deadline applies only to consignments over one tonne.
questions.explanation: The next sentence begins “Please raise them”, so the blank must introduce something that can be raised with a team leader — questions from customers. A visit by customs officers or a tonnage limit gives “them” nothing to refer to.
Leaving the yard is forbidden except on one condition, which is what “unless” expresses. “So that” would turn the attached reference into the purpose of the ban.

passages.label: Questions 135-138 refer to the following notice.
passages.content:
NOTICE TO RESIDENT GUESTS — LIFT REFURBISHMENT

The two guest lifts in the north wing will be out of service from 3 to 17 October while their control systems are replaced. {{135}} Signs at every landing will direct you to it.

Housekeeping will make an additional round of the north wing at 11 A.M. each day. Guests who need assistance {{136}} their luggage should call the front desk on extension 2, and a porter will be sent up.

We {{137}} that this work would cause the least disruption in October, when occupancy is at its lowest. Even so, guests on the upper floors may prefer a room closer to the ground. The duty manager will move you to the south wing at no extra charge, {{138}} to availability.

Thank you for your understanding.

Ilse Vandenberg, General Manager

choices: The service lift beside the kitchen will be open to guests for the duration of the work.
Both lifts were inspected by an external engineer in April.
The refurbishment will cost the group a considerable sum.
Guests are asked not to leave luggage on the landings.
questions.explanation: “Signs at every landing will direct you to it” needs a single alternative lift to point to, and only the service lift supplies one. April's inspection and the cost give “it” no antecedent.
“Assistance” takes “with” before the thing one is helped to handle: “assistance with their luggage”.
“Would cause” is the reported form of “will cause”, which requires a past reporting verb; the timing of the work has already been chosen.
The set phrase is “subject to availability”, meaning the move depends on a free room. “Owing to” would give availability as the reason for the move.

passages.label: Questions 139-142 refer to the following memo.
passages.content:
MEMORANDUM

To: Features and Production teams
From: Rosalía Marchetti, Managing Editor
Date: 9 February
Re: Spring issue deadlines

The printer has brought its schedule forward by a week, so the spring issue must be signed off on 6 March. All feature copy therefore needs to reach the subeditors' desk no {{139}} than 24 February.

Photography is the tightest part of the timetable. Anyone commissioning a shoot should obtain {{140}} approval from the picture desk before the fee is agreed, since we cannot process variations once a contract has been issued.

The picture desk has agreed to work through the weekend of 1 March, but that goodwill {{141}} on the rest of us filing on time. Please flag any image you know will need retouching as soon as you send in the copy that goes with it.

{{142}} The full timetable is pinned in the shared calendar.

questions.explanation: The comparative pattern “no later than” sets a deadline; “than” cannot follow the superlative “latest”.
A past participle works as an adjective before the noun: “written approval”, that is, approval given in writing.
The subject of the clause is the singular “goodwill”, so the verb takes the third-person -s.

choices: The printer has agreed to absorb the cost of the change.
I know these dates are tighter than usual, and I am grateful for the extra effort.
Please do not commission any new photography this quarter.
The spring issue will be twelve pages longer than the winter one.
questions.explanation: The memo has just asked for extra care under a compressed schedule, so a word of thanks closes it naturally before the pointer to the calendar. Banning new photography would contradict the paragraph that explains how to commission a shoot.

passages.label: Questions 143-146 refer to the following advertisement.
passages.content:
HALDEN HOUSE — Conference and Events Centre, Trondheim

Fifteen minutes from the airport and {{143}} reached by rail from the city centre, Halden House hosts residential meetings for ten to two hundred delegates.

Eight meeting rooms, every one of them with daylight and adjustable lighting. Day-delegate rates from €165 per person, including two breaks, a hot lunch and unlimited filter coffee. {{144}}

Our kitchen builds each menu around {{145}} the region's farms and boats supply that week, so the spring and autumn cards are never quite the same.

Residential delegates stay in one of forty rooms in the courtyard wing. Bookings of more than thirty rooms {{146}} a dedicated coordinator from the day the contract is signed.

Ask for our full pack: events@haldenhouse.example or +47 73 55 41 20.

questions.explanation: The blank modifies the participle “reached”, so an adverb is required: “easily reached by rail”.

choices: All rooms have been refurbished since the centre changed hands.
Parking is limited to twenty spaces in the summer season.
Evening meals and overnight accommodation are quoted separately.
Delegates are welcome to bring their own audiovisual equipment.
questions.explanation: The sentence before lists exactly what the day rate covers, so the natural follow-on states what it does not, and it leads into the paragraphs on dining and rooms.
The preposition “around” needs an object, and “what” both supplies it and heads the clause, meaning “the things that”. “Which” and “that” would need a noun to attach to.
The bookings receive a coordinator rather than allocating one, so the passive is needed: “are assigned a dedicated coordinator”.

parts.title: Reading Comprehension
parts.instructions: In this part you will read a selection of texts. Each text or set of texts is followed by several questions. Select the best answer for each question.

passages.label: Questions 147-148 refer to the following memo.
passages.content:
MEMORANDUM

To: All dock supervisors, Halvorsen Freight Terminal
From: Ingrid Solheim, Terminal Operations Manager
Date: 3 March
Subject: Bay assignments during resurfacing

The eastern yard will be resurfaced from 16 to 27 March. Bays 7 through 12 will be closed for the full two weeks, which leaves us nine working bays instead of fifteen.

To keep turnaround times under forty minutes, every inbound carrier must hold a booked arrival window for the duration of the works. Drivers who arrive without one will be asked to rebook, and that applies to the carriers we see every day as much as to anyone else. Please make this clear to them before the closure begins rather than at the gate.

Supervisors should also move the two afternoon container collections to the 6 A.M. slot, where the schedule has more room.

I will circulate the revised bay chart on 10 March.

questions.text: Why was the memo written?
choices: To introduce a booking system for warehouse customers
To explain how deliveries will be managed during resurfacing work
To announce a permanent reduction in the number of loading bays
To report a rise in the cost of terminal operations
questions.explanation: The memo announces a two-week closure of six bays and then sets out the arrangements — booked arrival windows and revised collection times — that will apply while the yard is resurfaced. The reduction is temporary, not permanent.

questions.text: What are supervisors asked to do about the afternoon container collections?
choices: Transfer them to a partner terminal
Move them to an early-morning slot
questions.explanation: “Supervisors should also move the two afternoon container collections to the 6 A.M. slot”. Nothing suggests the collections stop or are given to another terminal.

passages.label: Questions 149-150 refer to the following online chat discussion.
passages.content:
Priya Raghunathan (10:12) The printer has just called. The paper we specified for the Ostrowski cookbook is out of stock until mid-May.

Daniel Okonjo (10:14) That is three weeks after our launch date. Can they substitute?

Priya Raghunathan (10:15) They can, but only with a lighter stock. The photographs would lose a lot of their depth.

Daniel Okonjo (10:17) The photographs are the book. I would rather move the launch than print it on the wrong paper.

Priya Raghunathan (10:19) Marketing has already booked us into two food festivals on the last weekend in April.

Daniel Okonjo (10:21) Then they can rebook. Ask the printer to hold the original stock for us and I will speak to Marketing this afternoon.

Priya Raghunathan (10:22) Will do. I will let the studio know as well.

questions.text: At 10:17, what does Mr. Okonjo most likely mean when he writes, “The photographs are the book”?
choices: The images matter too much to risk a lower-quality paper
The book contains photographs but very little text
The photographer should be credited on the cover
The photographs have not yet been delivered
questions.explanation: Ms. Raghunathan has just said the substitute stock would cost the photographs their depth, and he answers by refusing to print on the wrong paper — so the remark is about how much the images are worth to the book.

questions.text: What does Mr. Okonjo agree to do?
choices: Discuss the schedule with the marketing team
questions.explanation: “I will speak to Marketing this afternoon” — the festivals they booked for April will have to be rearranged. It is Ms. Raghunathan, not Mr. Okonjo, who will contact the printer.

passages.label: Questions 151-153 refer to the following advertisement.
passages.content:
THE GRANARY AT ELDBERG — Events by the water

A restored 1890s grain store on the harbour front, twenty minutes from the airport, for conferences, receptions and product launches.

The Loft — seated 120, standing 200 — river-facing terrace
The Mill Room — seated 60, standing 90 — original timber beams

Weekday hire from €900, Saturday hire from €1,600. Bookings confirmed more than six months ahead are held at the current year's rates, whatever the increase in the meantime.

Viewings by appointment, Tuesday to Friday. Write to bookings@granaryeldberg.example.

questions.text: What does the hire of every room include?
questions.explanation: “Hire of any of the three rooms includes […] a technician on site for the whole of your booking”. The terrace belongs to The Loft alone, and outside caterers are expressly refused.

questions.text: Which room would suit a seated dinner for one hundred guests?
questions.explanation: Only The Loft seats more than one hundred, at 120. The Mill Room seats 60 and can take 90 only for a standing event, which a dinner is not.

questions.text: What is stated about bookings made well in advance?
choices: They are charged at this year's prices.
They may be cancelled without a fee.
questions.explanation: “Bookings confirmed more than six months ahead are held at the current year's rates”, so a later price rise does not reach them.

passages.label: Questions 154-156 refer to the following e-mail.
passages.content:
To: r.almeida@vestbyimports.example
From: claims@northgateforwarding.example
Date: 11 October
Subject: Consignment NG-448120

Dear Ms. Almeida,

Thank you for your message of 9 October about the twelve pallets of ceramic tableware that reached your Rotterdam warehouse with damaged outer packaging.

Our driver's handheld records show that the consignment left our Gdansk depot intact and was transferred to a partner vehicle at Hanover. We have asked that partner for its own loading photographs and expect them within three working days.

In the meantime, please do not dispose of the damaged cartons. A surveyor will visit your warehouse on 15 October to inspect them, and no claim can proceed without that inspection.

Once the surveyor's report reaches us, we will settle any confirmed loss within twenty-one days, in line with clause 9 of our carriage terms.

Yours sincerely,

Marek Zielinski
Claims Officer, Northgate Forwarding

questions.text: Why did Mr. Zielinski write the e-mail?
choices: To confirm a delivery date for a new consignment
To ask that damaged goods be returned to Gdansk
To explain how a complaint is being handled
To request payment of an overdue invoice
questions.explanation: He replies to Ms. Almeida's message about damaged packaging and sets out each step: the enquiry to the partner carrier, the surveyor's visit, then settlement. The cartons are to stay in Rotterdam, not go back to Gdansk.

questions.text: What is Ms. Almeida asked to do?
choices: Send a signed copy of clause 9
Keep the damaged cartons until 15 October
questions.explanation: “please do not dispose of the damaged cartons”, because the surveyor arrives on 15 October to inspect them. Northgate is dealing with the partner carrier itself.

questions.text: What does the e-mail suggest about the damage?
choices: It may have occurred after the goods left Gdansk.
It was limited to one of the twelve pallets.
It was caused by the driver's handheld device.
It has already been paid for in full.
questions.explanation: The records show the consignment leaving Gdansk intact, which points to something happening later — hence the request for the partner carrier's loading photographs from Hanover.

passages.label: Questions 157-159 refer to the following press release.
passages.content:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

Halden House to launch audio imprint

BERGEN, 5 June — Halden House, an independent publisher of travel and food writing, today announced Halden Audio, an imprint that will record titles from its backlist as well as new books.

— [1] — The first twelve recordings will be made in a studio the company has built inside its Bergen offices, rather than hired by the day as it has done until now. — [2] — Halden expects to release two audio titles a month from September.

“Our readers have been asking for this for years, and until now we could not answer them at a price that worked,” said Sofia Berntsen, managing director. — [3] —

The imprint will be led by Tomás Ferreira, who joins from a broadcasting background and will oversee narrator casting and studio scheduling. — [4] — Halden Audio titles will be sold through the company's own site and through the main audiobook retailers.

Media enquiries: press@haldenhouse.example

questions.text: What is stated about the first twelve recordings?
choices: They will be produced in a rented studio.
They will be made on the company's own premises.
They will all be new titles.
They will be released in a single month.
questions.explanation: The studio has been built “inside its Bergen offices, rather than hired by the day as it has done until now”. The imprint covers the backlist as well as new books, and releases come at two a month.

questions.text: What is indicated about Mr. Ferreira?
choices: He has written several travel books.
He will narrate the first twelve titles.
questions.explanation: He “joins from a broadcasting background”. His role is casting narrators and scheduling the studio, not reading the books himself.

questions.text: In which of the positions marked [1], [2], [3] and [4] does the following sentence best belong? “He takes up the post on 1 July.”
questions.explanation: “He” and “the post” need an appointment to refer back to, and the only one described is Mr. Ferreira's, in the sentence immediately before [4]. At [3] the nearest person named is Ms. Berntsen, who is already in her role.

passages.label: Questions 160-162 refer to the following text-message chain.
passages.content:
Amara Nwachukwu (16:41) I am at the Fjordlyng conference centre. The tables are laid for 90, which matches the guest list I was given, but the organiser tells me she is expecting 110.

Lukas Weber (16:44) The organiser added twenty places this morning. I sent the new list to your old address by mistake. Sorry.

Amara Nwachukwu (16:46) That explains it. Can the van bring twenty more covers and chairs? We have enough food.

Lukas Weber (16:49) Piotr is loading now. He can be with you by half past five.

Amara Nwachukwu (16:50) Cutting it fine. Doors at six.

Lukas Weber (16:52) Ask the centre for their stacking chairs as a fallback. They keep them behind the stage.

Amara Nwachukwu (16:55) Doing that now. If Piotr is on time we will not need them.

questions.text: Why was Ms. Nwachukwu unaware of the change to the guest list?
choices: The revised list went to an address she no longer uses.
She reached the venue after the tables had been laid.
The organiser made the change during the event.
The conference centre failed to pass on a message.
questions.explanation: “I sent the new list to your old address by mistake”, which is why she is still working from a list of 90.

questions.text: What does Mr. Weber suggest as a precaution?
choices: Delaying the start of the event
Reducing the number of courses served
questions.explanation: “Ask the centre for their stacking chairs as a fallback” — something to fall back on if Piotr is late. Ms. Nwachukwu confirms the food is sufficient, so the menu is not in question.

questions.text: At 16:50, what does Ms. Nwachukwu mean when she writes, “Cutting it fine”?
choices: The portions will have to be made smaller.
The van is carrying more than it should.
The guest list ought to be shortened.
The delivery will arrive with little time to spare.
questions.explanation: She follows the remark with “Doors at six”, and the van is due at half past five — only thirty minutes to set twenty extra places.

passages.label: Questions 163-165 refer to the following notice.
passages.content:

They will be asked to check out earlier than planned.
They may be offered a different room at no extra cost.
They will have breakfast brought to their rooms.

Luggage storage in the Harbour Room

questions.text: What is NOT mentioned in the notice as being affected by the work?
choices: Use of the north wing lifts

passages.label: Questions 166-169 refer to the following Web page.
passages.content:
www.kestrelline.example/services/bonded-storage

Kestrel Line — Bonded storage

Kestrel Line operates 18,000 square metres of customs-bonded warehousing at the Port of Trelleby. Goods held in a bonded facility are not taxed until they are released for sale, which frees capital while stock waits for a buyer.

What we hold
Palletised dry goods, wines and spirits, and packaged food with a shelf life of six months or more. We cannot accept chilled or frozen cargo, live plants, or hazardous material of any class.

What it costs
Storage is charged per pallet per week, from €4.10, with the rate falling once a customer keeps more than 200 pallets with us. Handling in and out is billed separately at €7.50 per pallet movement.

Reporting
Every customer receives a stock file each night and can also run the same report from the customer portal at any hour. Discrepancies raised before noon are investigated the same day.

To open an account, complete the enquiry form. Accounts are normally active within five working days.

questions.text: What advantage of bonded storage does the page describe?
choices: Handling is charged at a lower rate.
Tax is not due until the goods are sold.
questions.explanation: “Goods held in a bonded facility are not taxed until they are released for sale, which frees capital”. Handling is billed separately and at a flat rate.

questions.text: What kind of cargo will Kestrel Line accept?
questions.explanation: “wines and spirits” appear on the list of goods held. Frozen cargo, live plants and hazardous material are all excluded.

questions.text: In the section “What it costs”, the word “falling” is closest in meaning to
questions.explanation: The rate goes down for customers who store more than 200 pallets, so “falling” here means decreasing rather than collapsing, which would suggest a sudden failure.

questions.text: What is stated about stock reports?
choices: They are produced once a week.
Customers can generate them whenever they wish.
They must be requested before noon.
They are posted to the customer's office.
questions.explanation: Customers “can also run the same report from the customer portal at any hour”. Noon is the deadline for raising a discrepancy, not for asking for a report.

passages.label: Questions 172-175 refer to the following information.
passages.content:
TIDEWATER QUARTERLY — Subscriber information

They start with the following issue.
The announcement card goes to the buyer.

passages.label: Questions 181-185 refer to the following press release and article.
passages.content:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
Contact: Iwona Baran, Communications Manager — press@nordhaven.example

NORDHAVEN INTERMODAL OPENS KOLVIK RAIL TERMINAL

KOLVIK, 3 May — Nordhaven Intermodal today opened its fourth inland terminal, a 24-hectare rail-served facility 40 kilometres south of the port of Aalgard.

The site has two 750-metre loading tracks and capacity for 180,000 containers a year. Shuttle trains will run to the port six days a week, removing an estimated 62,000 lorry journeys from the coastal motorway annually.

“Customers have been asking us for an inland option since 2019,” said Petra Solheim, Chief Operating Officer. “Kolvik lets a container leave the quay in the evening and be ready for collection inland before breakfast.”

Construction took 19 months and cost €114 million, of which €31 million came from a regional transport fund. Ninety-four people have been recruited. A further 40 posts will follow when the second phase, a temperature-controlled warehouse, opens next spring.

passages.label: Questions 181-185 refer to the following press release and article.
passages.content:
Kolvik opens — but hauliers want the gate open longer
by Marek Ostrowski, Freight Quarterly, 11 May

Regional forwarders have given a guarded welcome to the container terminal that opened at Kolvik last week. The six-day shuttle to Aalgard was widely praised; the road gate was not.

At present the gate accepts road collections between 6 A.M. and 8 P.M. only. “If a box is ready for us before breakfast, we would like to collect it before breakfast,” said Anneke Ruys, who runs a forwarding firm in Bregge. “At the moment we cannot get through the gate until the morning peak has already started.”

Ms. Solheim told Freight Quarterly that a 24-hour gate was “under review” and that any decision would rest on the volumes handled in the first two quarters of operation. She declined to give a date.

The temperature-controlled warehouse remains on schedule for next spring.

questions.text: What is the purpose of the press release?
choices: To announce the opening of a new facility
To report the company's annual results
To advertise positions at a warehouse
To publish a revised shuttle train timetable
questions.explanation: The release exists to state that Nordhaven Intermodal “today opened its fourth inland terminal”. Recruitment and shuttle frequency are supporting details, not the announcement.

questions.text: What is planned for the second phase of the Kolvik site?
choices: A direct road link to the motorway
questions.explanation: “the second phase, a temperature-controlled warehouse, opens next spring”. The two loading tracks already exist.

questions.text: What is indicated about Ms. Solheim?
choices: She wrote the article for Freight Quarterly.
She runs a forwarding firm in Bregge.
She supervises the road gate at Kolvik.
She is Nordhaven Intermodal's chief operating officer.
questions.explanation: The article quotes her without a title; the press release identifies Petra Solheim as Chief Operating Officer of Nordhaven Intermodal.

questions.text: Why does Ms. Ruys mention breakfast?
choices: To propose a change to the shuttle train timetable
To show that the gate hours do not match a company claim
To praise the speed of the rail service to the port
To explain why her drivers begin work at night
questions.explanation: The press release promises a container “ready for collection inland before breakfast”, but the gate does not open until 6 A.M., so her remark points out the gap between the two.

questions.text: According to the article, what will determine whether the gate hours change?
choices: The volumes handled in the first two quarters
The completion of the second phase
A ruling by the regional transport fund
The number of staff recruited at the site
questions.explanation: Ms. Solheim says any decision “would rest on the volumes handled in the first two quarters of operation”. The warehouse is reported as on schedule but is not linked to the gate.

It has been added to her invoice.
questions.explanation: “One way only, please: […] I will make my own way to the airport on the Friday.” The invoice accordingly shows a single transfer.

questions.text: Which session will Ms. Ferreira most likely NOT attend?
questions.explanation: Her e-mail, sent well within the 48-hour limit for exchanges, asks to leave the menu-costing workshop for the Salon 2 session. She explicitly keeps the afternoon workshop.

questions.text: What does the accommodation line on the invoice suggest?
choices: Ms. Ferreira moved to a cheaper room type.
Ms. Ferreira checked in a day early.
Ms. Ferreira's Thursday night was not billed to the forum.
Ms. Ferreira shared a room with a colleague.
questions.explanation: The itinerary covers Tuesday and Wednesday nights, which is the two nights invoiced; the Thursday night she describes as private is therefore settled elsewhere, as the invoice's closing note indicates.

NORTHGATE AUDIO — audiobook production for independent publishers

A narrator from our open roster, one proof-listen, delivery in six weeks.

Signature — €62 per finished hour
Your choice of narrator from auditions by three readers, two proof-listens, delivery in four weeks.

passages.label: Questions 191-195 refer to the following advertisement, customer review, and response.
passages.content:
Reviewer: Ingrid Solvang, Larkfell Editions
Posted: 22 January
Rating: 4 out of 5

We recorded a four-book crime series with Northgate last autumn, and I would use them again — with one reservation.

At €55 per finished hour the rate was competitive for work of this quality, and the promise that mattered most to us was kept: one narrator read all four titles. Readers of a series notice a change of voice, and they complain about it.

Delivery is where it went wrong. The first title arrived on the agreed date. The fourth was eleven days late, and nobody told us — we found out because I wrote to ask. For a publisher with retailer listings already scheduled, that is expensive.

We also found a mispronounced place name in the second book. That was corrected within a week and we were not charged for it.

passages.label: Questions 191-195 refer to the following advertisement, customer review, and response.
passages.content:
Response from Daniel Okonkwo, Studio Manager, Northgate Audio
Posted: 26 January

Ms. Solvang, thank you for a review that is fair on both counts.

You are right about the fourth title. Our narrator was unavailable for a week in November, and we should have written to you on the day we knew rather than leaving you to ask. Since December every client receives an automatic message the moment a delivery date moves, whether it moves by a day or by a fortnight. That is a change we owe to your complaint and to two others like it.

On the correction in book two, I am glad it was straightforward — that is exactly what the clause is there for.

If Larkfell Editions returns to us this year, the studio time for your first title will be at no charge. Please write to me directly.

questions.text: What is included in all of Northgate Audio's prices?
choices: A choice of narrator from three auditions
Promotion of the finished title to retailers
questions.explanation: “Every price includes mastering to retail specification”. The three auditions and the four-week delivery belong to Signature only.

questions.text: What does the rate paid by Larkfell Editions indicate?
choices: The order was placed at the Signature rate.
The order qualified for the four-title price.
The files were delivered in six weeks.
questions.explanation: €55 per finished hour is the Series rate, which applies to orders of four titles or more — and Ms. Solvang recorded four books.

questions.text: What did Ms. Solvang value most about the work?
choices: That a single narrator read every book
That the studio answered her messages quickly
That the files arrived through a portal
That the rate was the lowest she had found
questions.explanation: “the promise that mattered most to us was kept: one narrator read all four titles”. She calls the rate competitive, not the lowest available.

questions.text: Why was the error in the second book corrected at no cost?
choices: The narrator agreed to work without a fee.
Larkfell Editions had ordered four titles.
Every Northgate price covers one short re-record.
The error was found before the file was delivered.
questions.explanation: The advertisement includes “one free re-record of up to fifteen minutes should you find an error after delivery”, which is the clause Mr. Okonkwo refers to. A single place name falls well inside fifteen minutes.

questions.text: What change has Northgate Audio made since December?
choices: It has raised the rate for extra re-recording.
It has doubled the size of its narrator roster.
It has shortened its standard delivery time.
It informs clients automatically when a date moves.
questions.explanation: “Since December every client receives an automatic message the moment a delivery date moves.” The free studio time is offered to Larkfell alone, not adopted as a policy.

To: b.lindqvist@rendellpark.example
From: operations@kestrelhaulage.example
Date: 9 June
Subject: Our deliveries during the resurfacing

We deliver to Rendell Park three times a week and I would like to get the fortnight right before I book the slots.

questions.text: What is the purpose of the notice?
choices: To announce a permanent change of address
To set out temporary arrangements during construction work
To advertise vacancies in the yard team
To introduce a charge for overnight parking
questions.explanation: Every instruction in the notice is limited to the two weeks of resurfacing, after which the yard reverts to normal.

questions.text: What are drivers required to do?
choices: Reserve an arrival time at least a day beforehand
Report to the driver facilities before unloading
Carry a printed copy of the notice

questions.text: What is indicated about the bay Kestrel Haulage normally uses?

It can be booked only through Ms. Lindqvist.
It is the bay closest to Gate 4.
It will be out of service for the whole fortnight.

They must be collected by another carrier.
They will be charged a fee at the overflow park.
