meta.notes: Complete Reading section in the official shape: Part 5 (30), Part 6 (16, four texts), Part 7 (54: ten single passages, two double, three triple). Numbered 101-200, 75 minutes.

parts.title: Incomplete Sentences
parts.instructions: A word or phrase is missing in each of the sentences below. Four answer choices are given. Select the best answer to complete the sentence.

questions.text: Warehouse staff at Solvenda Pharma record each incoming shipment ______ so that the month-end audit finds no discrepancies.
questions.explanation: The blank modifies the verb “record”, so an adverb is needed: “record each shipment carefully”.

questions.text: By the time the new distribution centre opens in March, Marleaux Retail ______ its warehouse team by nearly a third.
questions.explanation: “By the time” with a present-tense verb points to a future deadline, so the main clause takes the future perfect.

questions.text: All temperature-sensitive medicines must be moved to the cold room ______ thirty minutes of arrival.
questions.explanation: “Within thirty minutes” sets the time limit; “during” would need a named period rather than a deadline.

questions.text: The site manager submitted a ______ report on the delays affecting the foundation work.
questions.explanation: A modifier is required before the noun “report”, and the participial adjective “detailed” fills that slot.

questions.text: Prescription records ______ by two members of staff before they are filed.
questions.explanation: Records do not review anything; they undergo the action, so the present passive is required.

questions.text: The pharmacy's opening hours will be ______ during the refurbishment, with the counter closing at 4:00 P.M. instead of 7:00 P.M.
questions.explanation: Closing three hours earlier means the hours are shortened; “extended” states the opposite of what the sentence describes.

questions.text: Kestrel Homeware ______ its returns policy twice since the online store opened.
questions.explanation: “Since” plus a starting point calls for the present perfect: the two revisions fall in a period reaching the present.

questions.text: The scaffolding around the clinic's north facade is ______ secure, according to Thursday's safety inspection.
questions.explanation: An adverb is needed to modify the adjective “secure”; “structural” would have to sit before a noun.

questions.text: The architect ______ design won the civic centre competition will lead the hospital extension project.
questions.explanation: The design belongs to the architect, so the possessive relative “whose” is required; “who” would be followed by a verb, not by a noun.

questions.text: ______ the delivery van was held up by roadworks, the vaccines arrived within the required temperature range.
questions.explanation: The two clauses contrast, so a concessive conjunction is needed; “Despite” cannot introduce a clause with its own subject and verb.

questions.text: The contract requires the roof membrane to be guaranteed ______ a period of fifteen years.
questions.explanation: “For” introduces the length of a period; “during” would point to an event inside a period already identified.

questions.text: The dispensary has received formal ______ to store controlled medicines on the premises.
questions.explanation: The verb “received” needs a noun as its object: “received formal approval”.

questions.text: Employees who cannot attend Tuesday's safety briefing should notify ______ supervisor before Friday.
questions.explanation: A possessive determiner is needed before the noun “supervisor”; “theirs” stands alone and takes no noun after it.

questions.text: When the inspector arrived on Thursday, the electricians ______ the ground-floor wiring for two days.
questions.explanation: The work had been running for two days up to a moment in the past, which is what the past perfect continuous expresses.

questions.text: The procurement team recommends ______ the tender documents at least a week before the closing date.
questions.explanation: “Recommend” takes a gerund when no indirect object follows it; “to submit” would require a person in between.

questions.text: Ms. Ferreira asked the supplier to ______ the invoice, as two items had been charged twice.
questions.explanation: A duplicated charge is an error, so the invoice has to be corrected; approving it would leave the double charge in place.

questions.text: ______ of the cold-storage units is carried out every six months by a certified engineer.
questions.explanation: The subject of “is carried out” must be a noun.

questions.text: The contract for the hospital car park ______ to a firm based in Gdansk last month.
questions.explanation: The contract receives the action, and “last month” fixes it in finished past time, so the past passive is required.

questions.text: The prefabricated wall panels proved far ______ to install than the masonry design originally specified.
questions.explanation: “Than” signals a comparison of two things, so the comparative is required; “far” intensifies it.

questions.text: All suppliers must comply ______ the storage standards set out in Appendix 2.
questions.explanation: “Comply” is fixed with the preposition “with”.

questions.text: The revised floor plan is ______ with the fire regulations issued last year.
questions.explanation: After the linking verb “is”, an adjective is needed: “is consistent with”.

questions.text: The store will stay open throughout the refit ______ the paint fumes make it unsafe for customers.
questions.explanation: The clause names the single condition that would end the opening, which is what “unless” expresses; “in case” would describe a precaution taken in advance.

questions.text: The design team will begin the interior drawings as soon as the client ______ the revised budget.
questions.explanation: A time clause introduced by “as soon as” takes the present simple even when the reference is to the future.

questions.text: The refrigeration units ______ we ordered in April are still waiting for customs clearance.
questions.explanation: The relative pronoun refers to things and is the object of “ordered”, so “that” is required; “what” cannot follow the noun it describes.

questions.text: If the planning committee ______ the revised drawings next week, construction could start in October.
questions.explanation: A realistic future condition puts the present simple in the if-clause, with the modal in the main clause.

questions.text: Applicants for the pharmacy technician post must provide proof of professional ______.
questions.explanation: The preposition “of” and the adjective “professional” both call for a noun.

questions.text: Although the two shelving units look identical, one is ten centimetres deeper than ______.
questions.explanation: With exactly two items, the second one is “the other”; “another” would imply a third unit.

questions.text: The revised layout makes ______ use of the limited floor space behind the dispensary counter.
questions.explanation: Limited space calls for use that wastes nothing, which is what “efficient” describes.

questions.text: The building's ______ with the new accessibility code was confirmed during Monday's inspection.
questions.explanation: The subject of “was confirmed” is a noun phrase headed by “the building's”, so the noun “compliance” is required.

questions.text: Site visitors ______ wear a high-visibility jacket at all times in the loading area.
questions.explanation: A site rule states an obligation, which “must” conveys; “might” would reduce it to a possibility.

parts.title: Text Completion
parts.instructions: Read the texts that follow. A word, phrase, or sentence is missing in parts of each text. Select the best answer to complete the text.

passages.label: Questions 131-134 refer to the following letter.
passages.content:
Vesterlund Architects
17 Harbour Row, Portsmouth

12 October

Dr. Amara Okonkwo
Riverbend Community Health Centre

Dear Dr. Okonkwo,

Thank you for meeting us on site last Thursday. Following that visit, we have {{131}} the drawings for the outpatient extension to take account of your comments on the reception layout.

The new plan moves the waiting area away from the entrance doors, which should cut down draughts in winter. It also places a second consulting room {{132}} the dispensary and the staff room, so that both can be reached without crossing the waiting area. {{133}}, the storage cupboard you asked about has been widened to 1.8 metres.

We will submit the package to the planning office on 26 October. {{134}} If you would like anything changed before then, please let us know by 20 October.

Yours sincerely,

Henrik Vesterlund
Partner

questions.explanation: “We have” needs a past participle to complete the present perfect: “we have revised the drawings”.
Two rooms are named, and “between” is the preposition used with exactly two reference points; “among” would need three or more.
The cupboard is a further change on top of the ones just listed, so an additive transition is needed; “Instead” would mean it replaced them.

choices: The planning office rejected an earlier version of this scheme.
Construction of the extension was finished earlier this year.
We have therefore cancelled the site meeting arranged for that week.
A decision normally follows within eight weeks of submission.
questions.explanation: The sentence before gives the submission date, so a note on how long the decision takes continues the thought. A finished extension would make the whole letter pointless, and nothing in the letter suggests a rejection or a cancelled meeting.

passages.label: Questions 135-138 refer to the following e-mail.
passages.content:
To: All branch managers
From: Priya Raghunathan, Operations
Date: 3 February
Subject: Click-and-collect launch

Our click-and-collect service goes live in every branch on 1 March. {{135}} Customers will order online and pick their parcels up from a dedicated counter near the entrance.

Each branch will receive a shelving unit and a handheld scanner during the week of 17 February. Please make sure the counter area has been cleared {{136}} the delivery arrives, as the units are two metres wide.

Parcels {{137}} within four hours of an order being placed. Customers are sent a text message the moment their parcel is ready, so the four-hour window matters.

A short training video will be circulated next week; please watch it with your team before 1 March. By the end of that month we expect that every branch {{138}} at least fifty collections a week.

choices: The pilot in our three largest stores has run since November without difficulty.
The service will be limited to branches in the northern region.
Online orders will no longer be accepted after that date.
Parcels must be returned to the supplier within seven days.
questions.explanation: A reference to the pilot supports the launch announcement it follows. Limiting the service to one region contradicts “every branch”, and ending online orders would remove the reason for the counter described next.
The clearing has to happen ahead of the delivery, which “before” expresses; “during” cannot introduce a clause with a subject and verb.
Parcels are acted on rather than acting, so the passive is required after the modal.
“By the end of that month” looks forward from a launch still to come, so a future form is needed.

passages.label: Questions 139-142 refer to the following web page.
passages.content:
Nordhelm Pharmacy Services — Home Delivery

Repeat prescriptions {{139}} are issued by any surgery in the Larkfield district can now be delivered to your door. Delivery is free on orders above $20 and costs $3.50 otherwise.

To register, create an account and enter the name of the surgery that holds your records. Once your details {{140}} by our team, you can request a delivery from your dashboard at any time.

Deliveries run Monday to Saturday between 9 A.M. and 6 P.M. {{141}} Refrigerated items travel in insulated boxes and are handed over in person; they are never left with a neighbour.

If you will not be at home, you can {{142}} a delivery to the following day at no extra charge, provided you tell us before 8 P.M. the evening before.

questions.explanation: The relative pronoun stands for “prescriptions”, which are things, and introduces a clause describing them: “prescriptions that are issued”.
The details undergo the checking, so a passive form is needed, and the perfect shows the checking is complete before a delivery can be requested.

choices: You may choose a two-hour slot when you place your order.
Orders placed on Sunday are delivered the same afternoon.
Our couriers cannot carry medicines that need refrigeration.
The district's only pharmacy closed at the end of last year.
questions.explanation: A note on choosing a slot develops the delivery-hours sentence it follows. Sunday delivery contradicts the Monday-to-Saturday schedule, and refusing refrigerated items contradicts the sentence immediately after the blank.
“To the following day” shows the delivery is moved rather than dropped, which is what “postpone” means.

passages.label: Questions 143-146 refer to the following memo.
passages.content:
MEMORANDUM

To: All staff, Meridian Heights Medical Centre
From: Facilities Office
Date: 9 June
Subject: Car park resurfacing, 22-26 June

The main staff car park {{143}} for five days from Monday 22 June while the surface is replaced.

During that week, staff should use the overflow area behind the laundry building. {{144}} Spaces there are limited, so please share transport where you can.

The contractor will start work at 7 A.M. each day. Noise will be {{145}} noticeable in the ground-floor offices on the east side, and colleagues based there are welcome to work from Room 118 instead.

We apologise for the disruption. Anyone who needs a reserved space for mobility reasons should contact the facilities office by 15 June so that one can be {{146}}.

questions.explanation: The closure starts on a date still ahead of the 9 June memo, and the car park is acted on, so the future passive is required.

choices: The laundry building will also be shut to staff that week.
A shuttle will run from there to the main entrance every fifteen minutes.
Visitors may continue to park in the main car park as usual.
The new surface will be laid in a single day.
questions.explanation: The shuttle explains how staff get from the overflow area to the building, following directly from the instruction to park there. Open access to the main car park and a one-day job both contradict the announcement.
An adverb is needed to modify the adjective “noticeable”.
After “can be”, a past participle forms the passive: the space is arranged by the office, not by the person asking.

parts.title: Reading Comprehension
parts.instructions: In this part you will read a selection of texts. Each text or set of texts is followed by several questions. Select the best answer for each question.

passages.label: Questions 147-148 refer to the following notice.
passages.content:
NOTICE TO ALL DEPARTMENT COORDINATORS

The Central Supply collection window on Level 1 of the Kirkvale Health Centre will be closed from 11 to 22 May while the corridor floor is replaced. During this period, collections will be handled at the Loading Bay B counter, which is entered from the rear car park.

Requests received after 3:00 P.M. will be held until the following working day.

Ilona Bergqvist, Supply Services Manager

questions.text: What is the purpose of the notice?
choices: To introduce a new system for ordering supplies
To announce a temporary change to a collection point
To recruit additional staff for a supply department
To explain an increase in the cost of supplies
questions.explanation: The notice announces that the Level 1 window closes from 11 to 22 May and that collections move to Loading Bay B for that period. Nothing in it changes how supplies are ordered — standing orders continue unchanged.

questions.text: What should a coordinator do to receive an extra item on the same day?
choices: Go to the Level 1 window in person
Add the item to the ward's standing order
Collect the item from the rear car park before noon
Telephone the supply department before 3:00 P.M.
questions.explanation: “should telephone extension 4180 before 3:00 P.M. so that it can be brought to Loading Bay B the same afternoon”. Requests made later wait until the next working day.

passages.label: Questions 149-150 refer to the following text-message chain.
passages.content:
Dariusz Wieczorek (8:42 A.M.)
The tile shipment for the Halverson lobby is at the gate. The driver's paperwork says 60 boxes, but our manifest says 48.

Priya Raghunathan (8:45 A.M.)
48 is what I ordered. The extra 12 must be the stair nosing that was meant to go to the Fenwick site.

Dariusz Wieczorek (8:47 A.M.)
Do I send those back with him?

Priya Raghunathan (8:49 A.M.)
No. Fenwick is twenty minutes away and their crew starts on Thursday. Sign for all 60 and I will take the twelve across in the van tomorrow.

Dariusz Wieczorek (8:51 A.M.)
Understood. I will keep them on the pallet by the hoist so nobody opens them.

questions.text: What problem does Mr. Wieczorek report?
choices: A delivery contains more boxes than expected.
A shipment has arrived later than scheduled.
Several boxes were damaged in transit.
An order was never placed with the supplier.
questions.explanation: The driver's paperwork lists 60 boxes while the site manifest lists 48, so twelve more boxes have turned up than were ordered.

questions.text: What will most likely happen tomorrow?
choices: The driver will return to the gate for a collection.
The Fenwick crew will begin work on the lobby.
Ms. Raghunathan will move twelve boxes to another site.
The stair nosing will be unpacked beside the hoist.
questions.explanation: “I will take the twelve across in the van tomorrow” — across to Fenwick, whose crew starts on Thursday. Mr. Wieczorek stores the boxes by the hoist precisely so that they are not opened.

passages.label: Questions 151-153 refer to the following job posting.
passages.content:
NORDHAVEN PHARMACEUTICALS
Cold Chain Logistics Coordinator — Vantaa distribution centre

Nordhaven Pharmaceuticals supplies temperature-sensitive products to hospital pharmacies in fourteen countries. We are seeking a Cold Chain Logistics Coordinator for our distribution centre in Vantaa.

The role: planning refrigerated shipments, monitoring temperature data loggers, and acting as the first point of contact for carriers when a consignment is delayed. The coordinator reports to the Distribution Manager and works alongside two schedulers.

Requirements
— Three years' experience in warehousing or freight forwarding
— Working knowledge of temperature-controlled distribution
— Fluent English; a second European language is an advantage
— Willingness to be on call one weekend in five

We offer a salary from $52,000, subsidised canteen meals and thirty days of annual leave. A candidate who does not yet hold a certificate in good distribution practice will be enrolled in a funded course during the first year.

Send a curriculum vitae and a covering letter naming two referees to careers@nordhavenpharma.example by 30 September. Interviews will be held in Vantaa in the second week of October; travel costs are reimbursed.

questions.text: What is indicated about the position?
choices: It is offered on a temporary contract.
It can be carried out from any of fourteen countries.
questions.explanation: “Willingness to be on call one weekend in five” appears among the requirements. The coordinator works alongside the two schedulers, not above them.

questions.text: What is stated about a second European language?
choices: It must be certified before the interview.
It is tested during the first year of employment.
It raises the starting salary above $52,000.
It is useful but not required.
questions.explanation: “Fluent English; a second European language is an advantage” — an advantage, not a requirement. Only English fluency is obligatory.

questions.text: Why does the posting mention a funded course?
choices: To indicate that a certificate is not needed at the time of hiring
To explain why the salary begins at $52,000
To describe a benefit available to every employee
To set out a condition for being invited to an interview
questions.explanation: The course is offered to “a candidate who does not yet hold a certificate”, which tells applicants they may apply without one. It is not open to all staff, only to those lacking the qualification.

passages.label: Questions 154-156 refer to the following letter.
passages.content:
Vestbury Architects
17 Calderwood Row
Portmarrow

12 June

Ms. Adaeze Okonkwo
Facilities Director
Larkfield Community Trust

Dear Ms. Okonkwo,

Thank you for sending the survey drawings for the annexe at Larkfield Hall. Our structural engineer has now reviewed them.

The drawings confirm that the north wall can carry the proposed second storey without additional piling, which removes the largest cost risk we identified in April. However, the survey stops at the boundary line, and the drainage run serving the annexe appears to continue beneath the neighbouring car park. Before we can complete the planning submission we will need written confirmation from the car park's owner that the run may stay where it is.

I have therefore held the drawing package at stage C instead of taking it to stage D, so that we do not have to redraw the ground floor twice.

Could you tell me by 26 June whether your legal team can obtain that confirmation? If it is likely to take more than a month, I would suggest submitting the annexe and the drainage works as two separate applications.

Yours sincerely,

Tomás Berenguer
Project Architect

questions.text: What did the survey drawings establish?
choices: That the annexe will have to be demolished
That additional piling must be installed
That the north wall can support another storey
That the boundary line was recorded incorrectly
questions.explanation: “The drawings confirm that the north wall can carry the proposed second storey without additional piling”. Piling is what the drawings rule out, not what they require.

questions.text: Why has Mr. Berenguer held the work at stage C?
choices: An invoice from his practice remains unpaid.
The structural engineer has not finished the review.
A planning application has already been refused.

Timber returns to the city centre

By Delphine Arroyo

Until recently, an eight-storey office block in this country meant steel and concrete. That is changing. Nineteen buildings of five storeys or more framed in cross-laminated timber were completed nationally last year, against three in the year the material was first permitted at that height.

Developers give two reasons. The panels arrive cut to size, so a floor can be assembled in days rather than in weeks, and a timber frame weighs roughly a fifth of a concrete one, which cuts the cost of foundations on soft ground.

Tenants appear to have noticed. Letting agents report that timber schemes are being taken up before completion at a rate the sector has not seen for a decade.

Not everyone is persuaded. Insurers have been slow to price the risk, and several city authorities still ask for fire modelling beyond what the building code requires. “The engineering is settled,” says Ravi Mahadevan of the practice Norrland & Vale. “The paperwork is not.”

questions.text: By what date must invoice 7742 be paid?

questions.text: Why does Ms. Marchetti believe Thermaline owes her something?

She was charged for delivery she should not have paid for.
One of the twelve shippers arrived damaged.
Fewer coolant packs were supplied than advertised.

questions.text: What is true of the order Ms. Marchetti is considering?
choices: It will not qualify for the volume rate.
It will be larger than the September order.
It will be for the same model as the September order.
It will have to be paid for when it is placed.
questions.explanation: The 8% volume rate begins at ten units of one model, and she intends to buy six. Six units is fewer than the twelve she bought in September, and of a different model.

parts.title: Incomplete Sentences
parts.instructions: A word or phrase is missing in each of the sentences below. Four answer choices are given. Select the best answer to complete the sentence.

questions.text: The new interface is ______ simple, which is why most agents need only an hour of training.
questions.explanation: An adverb is needed to modify the adjective “simple”: “deceptively simple”.

questions.text: By the time the autumn harvest begins, Vasterlund Orchards ______ the installation of its new sorting line.
questions.explanation: “By the time … begins” sets a deadline in the future, so the future perfect is required for something finished before that point.

questions.text: All exhibit labels must reach the design office ______ 15 March so that printing can begin.
questions.explanation: “by 15 March” states a deadline. “Until” would describe an action continuing up to that date, which a single delivery cannot do.

questions.text: The redesigned dashboard gives packhouse supervisors ______ access to yield figures from every line.
questions.explanation: “Instant access” is the standard collocation for data available with no delay; “abrupt” and “hasty” describe something done suddenly or carelessly, not availability.

questions.text: The curator recommended ______ the textile display until the humidity controls have been serviced.
questions.explanation: “Recommend” takes a gerund when no object follows: “recommended postponing the display”.

questions.text: The gallery's lighting system operates ______ during opening hours, dimming as the daylight changes.
questions.explanation: The verb “operates” needs an adverb to say how it works: “operates automatically”.

questions.text: ______ of the two candidates for the archivist post has worked with digitised collections.
questions.explanation: “Of the two” with the singular verb “has” points to “Either”; “Both” would require the plural “have”.

questions.text: Northfield Dairy ______ its packaging supplier three times since the plant opened.
questions.explanation: “Since the plant opened” marks a period running up to the present, which the present perfect expresses.

questions.text: Ticket holders were ______ to learn that the sculpture wing would stay closed for a further week.
questions.explanation: The people experience the feeling, so the past participle is used: “holders were disappointed”. “Disappointing” would describe the news rather than the holders.

questions.text: Delegates found the conference app surprisingly ______, even on five-year-old handsets.
questions.explanation: In “find + object + complement”, the complement describes the app, so the adjective “reliable” is needed.

questions.text: Attendance at the weekend workshops rose sharply ______ the second quarter.
questions.explanation: A stretch of time takes “during”: “during the second quarter”. “Between” would need two separate points in time.

questions.text: The list of approved seed varieties ______ updated every January by the regional agency.
questions.explanation: The subject is the singular “list”, not “varieties”, so the singular “is” is correct.

questions.text: The museum has ______ a grant of $85,000 to conserve its collection of glass negatives.
questions.explanation: “Secure a grant” means to obtain funding after applying for it; “gather” and “collect” suit objects one accumulates, and “reach” suits a target or an agreement.

questions.text: The laboratory is looking for an experienced ______ to lead its soil-testing programme.
questions.explanation: The sentence describes a person to be hired, so the person noun “analyst” is needed; “analysis” names the activity.

questions.text: Photographs of the excavation ______ in the east corridor until the end of the year.
questions.explanation: The photographs receive the action rather than perform it, so a passive form is required, and the period runs into the future.

questions.text: When the auditors arrived on Tuesday, the finance team ______ the quarterly figures for six hours.
questions.explanation: The review was already under way when the auditors arrived, and the duration “for six hours” calls for the past perfect continuous.

questions.text: ______ the irrigation contract was signed late, the pilot plots were planted on schedule.
questions.explanation: Two contrasting clauses need the subordinating conjunction “Although”; “Despite” must be followed by a noun phrase rather than a clause.

questions.text: The IT department has arranged ______ every workstation with the new client before the audit.
questions.explanation: “Arrange” is followed by an infinitive: “has arranged to update”.

questions.text: Growers reported a significant ______ in water use after switching to drip irrigation.
questions.explanation: After the article and adjective “a significant”, a noun is required: “a significant reduction in”.

questions.text: There is very ______ evidence that the new coating shortens shelf life.
questions.explanation: “Evidence” is uncountable and so takes “little”; the other three quantifiers require a countable plural noun.

questions.text: Under the revised licence, the software may be installed ______ up to five devices per user.
questions.explanation: Software is installed “on” a device, so “installed on up to five devices” is the correct phrasing.

questions.text: The catalogue entry was ______ after new evidence about the painting's origin came to light.
questions.explanation: A description corrected in the light of new evidence is “revised”; “revoked” applies to permissions and “reversed” to decisions.

questions.text: The vineyard was replanted under the ______ of an agronomist from Mendoza.
questions.explanation: “Under the supervision of” is the fixed phrase, and only the noun “supervision” fits between “the” and “of” here.

questions.text: The support desk ______ more than two hundred tickets last Thursday, a record for a single day.
questions.explanation: “Last Thursday” is a finished past time, which requires the simple past; the present perfect cannot be used with it.

questions.text: The second prototype proved ______ to assemble than the one the team built in the spring.
questions.explanation: “Than” requires a comparative, and “far easier” is the only choice that supplies one.

questions.text: The samples ______ from the northern plots will be tested before the others.
questions.explanation: A reduced relative clause is needed — “the samples that were collected” — so the past participle is correct; “collecting” would make the samples do the collecting.

questions.text: The festival's ______ director will announce next season's programme in April.
questions.explanation: The noun “director” needs an adjective in front of it, and “artistic director” is the established title.

questions.text: Neither the projector nor the speakers ______ working when the lecture was due to begin.
questions.explanation: After “neither … nor”, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, the plural “speakers”, and the lecture is in the past.

questions.text: Because the server room is locked outside office hours, contractors ______ arrange access a day in advance; no exceptions will be made.
questions.explanation: “No exceptions will be made” signals an obligation rather than a possibility or a permission, so “must” is the only fit.

questions.text: All applicants will be notified of the panel's ______ by the end of May.
questions.explanation: The possessive “panel's” must be followed by a noun: “the panel's decision”.

parts.title: Text Completion
parts.instructions: Read the texts that follow. A word, phrase, or sentence is missing in parts of each text. Select the best answer to complete the text.

passages.label: Questions 131-134 refer to the following memo.
passages.content:
MEMORANDUM

To: All Helpdesk Staff
From: Priya Raghunathan, Service Operations
Date: 12 May
Subject: Change to ticket triage

From Monday 19 May, incoming tickets will no longer be assigned by hand. The routing engine will read each request and {{131}} it to the queue that matches the system being reported. Tickets the engine cannot classify will land in a general queue, which the duty lead checks twice a day.

We expect the change to {{132}} the first-response time for common requests, which currently wait an average of forty minutes. During the first fortnight, please make a note of any ticket that reaches the wrong queue. {{133}} The vendor has agreed to retrain the classifier at the end of June using everything we send.

One thing does not change: the {{134}} of a ticket is still decided by the agent who picks it up, not by the routing engine.

questions.explanation: The blank continues “will read each request and ______”, so the bare infinitive “direct” is needed to match “read”.
A length of time is “shortened”; “shrink” applies to physical size, “abbreviate” to words and “compress” to files.

choices: Agents should keep assigning tickets by hand until further notice.
A short form for reporting these cases is now on the intranet.
The routing engine will be switched off for the whole of June.
The vendor no longer supports the classifier we are using.
questions.explanation: The sentence before asks staff to note mis-routed tickets and the one after refers to what the team sends the vendor, so a sentence explaining how to report them belongs here. Keeping manual assignment or switching the engine off would contradict the memo.
Between “the” and “of” a noun is required: “the priority of a ticket”.

passages.label: Questions 135-138 refer to the following e-mail.
passages.content:
To: Members of the Vale Growers' Association
From: Bendik Sørland, Field Services
Date: 3 February
Subject: Free soil testing — March round

Our March round of free soil testing is now open to every member farm. {{135}} Sampling kits will be posted to the address we hold on file, so please check that yours is up to date.

Each kit contains ten tubes, a probe and a prepaid return envelope. Take one sample from every hectare you intend to test, and {{136}} the tubes clearly with the name of the plot. Results take about twelve working days from the day the laboratory receives your package.

This year the report also {{137}} an estimate of organic matter, which a number of you asked for last season. There is no charge for the addition. Results are sent {{138}} e-mail only; we no longer post paper copies.

To register, reply to this message before 20 February.

choices: Farms that joined the association after September are eligible for the first time.
The testing service has been suspended until further notice.
A fee of $60 per kit applies to every participant this year.
Only farms in the northern district may take part in this round.
questions.explanation: The sentence announces that the round is open to every member farm, so a note about who is newly eligible follows naturally. A fee contradicts “free” and “no charge”, and a district restriction contradicts “every member farm”.
The blank continues the imperative “Take one sample …, and ______”, so the base form “label” is required.
The singular subject “the report” takes the singular present verb “includes”.
The means by which something is transmitted takes “by”: “sent by e-mail”.

passages.label: Questions 139-142 refer to the following information.
passages.content:
MEMBERSHIP RENEWAL — WHAT HAPPENS NEXT

Thank you for renewing your membership of the Ardmore Institute of Applied Arts. Your new card will reach you within ten working days. {{139}} it does, the confirmation e-mail you received serves as proof of membership at the admissions desk.

Members enter all permanent galleries free of charge and receive two guest passes a year. The passes are valid on any day except the opening weekend of a {{140}} exhibition, when demand is at its highest.

Your card also gives you fifteen percent off in the shop and the café. Places on the Thursday evening lecture series {{141}} to members a week before general booking opens, and the room seats sixty.

If your card has not arrived after ten working days, please write to members@ardmoreinstitute.example. {{142}} Replacement cards are issued free of charge.

questions.explanation: The e-mail serves as proof only for the period before the card arrives, so the time conjunction “Until” is correct.
The noun “exhibition” needs an adjective in front of it, and only “temporary” is an adjective.
Places do not offer themselves; the institute offers them to members, so the passive “are offered” is required.

choices: Membership cards cannot be replaced once they have been issued.
Please include the postcode the card was sent to.
The institute no longer accepts renewals by post.
Guest passes must be collected from the shop in person.
questions.explanation: The paragraph deals with a card that has not arrived, so asking for the delivery postcode helps trace it. The sentence that follows promises free replacements, which rules out the claim that cards cannot be replaced.

passages.label: Questions 143-146 refer to the following notice.
passages.content:
NOTICE — SCHEDULED SYSTEM MAINTENANCE

The stock and ordering system will be unavailable from 22:00 on Friday 6 June until 06:00 on Saturday 7 June while the database is moved to new hardware. All twelve packhouses, including the two that joined the network in April, {{143}} affected.

Supervisors should print the Saturday morning picking lists before they leave on Friday. {{144}} Orders taken by telephone during the outage must be written on the paper forms kept in each office and entered on Monday.

We have chosen this window because it is the {{145}} period of the week for order traffic. Even so, some of you will be working, and we are sorry for the inconvenience.

Questions about the move should go to Ingrid Halvorsen, {{146}} will monitor the migration overnight and can be reached on extension 4102.

questions.explanation: The subject is the plural “packhouses” — the phrase between the commas does not change it — and the outage has not happened yet, so “will be affected” is the only possible form.

choices: The new hardware will be installed at head office in July.
Picking lists can be generated from the mobile app at any time.
Nothing printed after 22:00 will show the final order figures.
Saturday deliveries have been cancelled for this weekend.
questions.explanation: The instruction to print before Friday evening needs a reason, and a printout made during the migration would be out of date. Generating lists from the app is impossible while the system is down, and the paragraph shows that Saturday orders are still being taken.
“Of the week” sets the whole week as the field of comparison, which calls for the superlative “quietest”.
A relative clause about a person, with the pronoun acting as the subject of “will monitor”, takes “who”; “whom” would be needed only for an object.

passages.label: Questions 147-148 refer to the following information.
passages.content:
HARVEST NOTE — Week 24
Included with every Torvald Fields vegetable box

This week's box was packed on Tuesday morning at our sorting shed in Reddington and left the same afternoon. Everything in it was cut, pulled or picked within forty-eight hours of packing.

In the box: broad beans, red chard, spring onions, two heads of butter lettuce, 500 g of new potatoes and a bunch of flat-leaf parsley.

A note on the potatoes. The wet spring pushed our own main crop back by roughly three weeks, so this week's potatoes come from Bendik Aasen's farm in the next valley, which sits on lighter soil and drained faster. They are grown to the same standard as ours and cost us slightly more; we have absorbed the difference rather than change your subscription price.

Recipe cards are no longer printed. Every recipe we have ever sent out is at torvaldfields.example/kitchen, sorted by vegetable.

Questions about a delivery? Reply to the message that told you your box was on its way.

questions.text: Why does the note mention Bendik Aasen's farm?
choices: To announce the closure of a nearby farm
To explain where one item in the box came from
To recommend a shop in the next valley
To introduce a new subscription level
questions.explanation: A wet spring delayed Torvald Fields' own potatoes, so the potatoes in this week's box were bought from the neighbouring farm instead.

questions.text: What change does the note describe?
choices: The box is now packed on a different day.
Deliveries are now confirmed by telephone.
Recipes are provided online rather than on paper.
questions.explanation: “Recipe cards are no longer printed” and every recipe is now on the website. The price is tempting because the potatoes cost more, but the note says that difference was absorbed.

passages.label: Questions 149-150 refer to the following online chat discussion.
passages.content:
Priya Raghunathan (10:02) — The staging server is refusing every deploy this morning. Is anyone else seeing this?

Marek Wozniak (10:04) — Yes. It started around 09:30. The build passes and then the upload step times out.

Priya Raghunathan (10:05) — So it is not something we wrote.

Ines Ferreira (10:09) — It is not. Hosting rotated the storage credentials overnight and did not tell us. Our deploy key is dead.

Marek Wozniak (10:10) — Can we generate a new one ourselves?

Ines Ferreira (10:12) — Only from the account owner's console, and that is Daniel, who is away until Thursday. I have opened a ticket and marked it urgent.

Priya Raghunathan (10:13) — The client demonstration is at 14:00. I will run it from the build already on production and say nothing.

Ines Ferreira (10:14) — That works. Nothing in this week's changes affects what they asked to see.

questions.text: What is causing the deployment failures?
choices: The hosting provider changed the storage credentials.
The team's most recent code contains an error.
The staging server has run out of space.
A scheduled maintenance window was missed.
questions.explanation: “Hosting rotated the storage credentials overnight […] Our deploy key is dead.” The code is not at fault, since the build itself passes.

questions.text: At 10:14, what does Ms. Ferreira most likely mean when she writes, “That works”?
choices: A new deploy key has been issued.
The provider has already resolved the ticket.
She agrees that the demonstration can use the older build.
She will reach Daniel before Thursday.
questions.explanation: She is replying to Ms. Raghunathan's plan to show the client the build already on production, and she adds that the week's changes are irrelevant to the demonstration.

passages.label: Questions 151-153 refer to the following advertisement.
passages.content:

A guest pass for every visit

choices: They collect their card at the museum.
They cannot enter the permanent galleries until January.
They must apply again in the following season.

To give the date of the reopening
To announce when the ticketed exhibitions open
To explain when membership cards are posted

passages.label: Questions 154-156 refer to the following e-mail.

To: r.oyelaran@ferrolinelogistics.example

choices: Reduce the number of records in her account
Reschedule her exports for a later date
Run exports by hand from the Reports screen
Contact the engineer who wrote the fix
questions.explanation: “exports started by hand from the Reports screen are unaffected, so please use that route for anything urgent”. Contacting the engineer is offered only if the corrected files fail to open.

questions.text: What has been done about the two faulty exports?
choices: They have been deleted from the account.
They were attached to this message.
They were replaced with the versions from 6 May.
Corrected copies were added to the Files area.

It will be delayed until the fix is released.
It will include a charge for the corrected files.
questions.explanation: It will be issued “at half the usual amount” and “You do not need to request this” — a reduction applied automatically, not a cancellation.

passages.label: Questions 157-159 refer to the following article.
passages.content:
Sensors move into the greenhouse
By Adaeze Nwachukwu

Until recently the tomato growers of the Vale district judged their crop as their parents had: by hand, by eye, and by walking the rows twice a day. Since March, four of the district's largest producers have been running a system that does part of that walking for them.

Built by a small firm in the regional capital, the system buries a probe every twenty metres and reports soil moisture, temperature and salinity to a screen in the packing shed. Growers set a range for each figure, and when a reading leaves that range a message is sent.

The saving is not in labour. Ola Bergström, who grows twelve hectares under glass, says his staff still walk the rows. What has changed is water. “We were irrigating on a schedule,” he said. “Now we irrigate when the soil asks for it. That has cut our use by about a fifth.”

Whether smaller growers will follow is less certain. Installation runs to roughly $9,000 per hectare, and the district's co-operative has so far declined to subsidise it.

questions.text: What does the system report to the packing shed?
questions.explanation: The buried probes send “soil moisture, temperature and salinity” to a screen in the packing shed.

questions.text: The word “declined” in the last paragraph is closest in meaning to
questions.explanation: “Declined to subsidise it” means the co-operative has refused to pay towards the cost. “Reduced” and “descended” are the other senses of the verb and do not work before an infinitive.

questions.text: What is implied about the cost of the system?
choices: It falls a little each year.
It is met by the district's co-operative.
It is lower than the cost of hiring extra staff.
It may prevent smaller growers from adopting the system.
questions.explanation: The doubt about smaller growers is stated immediately before the figure of $9,000 per hectare and the co-operative's refusal to help, so price is presented as the obstacle. The article says the saving is not in labour.

passages.label: Questions 160-162 refer to the following text-message chain.
passages.content:
Hana Okabe (08:41)
The crate with the Weiss panels is here, but the truck is at the loading bay on Mill Street, not the one on Carrow Lane.

Tobias Adeyemi (08:43)

It is too small for the crate.

choices: Take delivery of the crate at the Carrow Lane bay
Unwrap the panels in the corridor

questions.text: At 08:49, what does Mr. Adeyemi imply when he writes, “Nothing gets unwrapped in the corridor again”?

The conservator prefers to work without an audience.
Opening a crate outside a gallery has caused trouble before.
The panels have already been inspected once.
questions.explanation: “Again” points back to an earlier occasion, and he insists the crate go straight to Gallery 3 before anyone opens it.

passages.label: Questions 163-165 refer to the following memo.
passages.content:
MEMORANDUM

To: All shift supervisors, Line 2
From: Ingrid Halvorsen, Plant Manager
Date: 9 November
Subject: Changeover procedure

From Monday 16 November, Line 2 will run oat drinks on the early shift and almond drinks on the late shift. The two products cannot share equipment without a full wash, and the wash is what this memo is about.

Until now the outgoing shift has begun the wash and the incoming shift has finished it. That arrangement has twice produced a line signed off as clean when it was not. From Monday the wash belongs to a single shift from start to finish: the outgoing shift runs it, records the readings and signs the sheet before anyone from the next shift touches the line.

This adds thirty-five minutes to the end of each shift. The extra time is paid and has been agreed with the works council.

Supervisors should collect the revised sheets from my office this week. The old sheets will be taken off the line on Friday.

questions.text: What is the main purpose of the memo?
choices: To announce a new product line
To report the findings of an inspection
To ask for volunteers to work extra shifts
To set out a change to a cleaning procedure
questions.explanation: The subject line is “Changeover procedure”, and the memo is given over to the new rule that one shift now performs the whole wash.

questions.text: What problem does Ms. Halvorsen say the previous arrangement caused?
choices: A line was signed off as clean when it was not.
Two shifts were paid for the same work.
Products were packed into the wrong containers.
questions.explanation: Splitting the wash between two shifts “has twice produced a line signed off as clean when it was not”.

questions.text: What are supervisors asked to do this week?
choices: Train the late shift on Line 2
questions.explanation: “Supervisors should collect the revised sheets from my office this week.” The agreement with the works council is already in place.

passages.label: Questions 166-169 refer to the following web page.
passages.content:
halversenglass.example  ›  For professionals  ›  Object loans

Loans from the collection

The Halversen lends objects from its permanent collection to museums, galleries and registered public archives. We do not lend to private collectors, to commercial premises, or for use as film or photographic props. — [1]

Requests must reach the registrar at least nine months before the opening date of the exhibition. — [2] A request should name the objects by catalogue number, state the dates on which the objects would be away from us, and describe the case or mount in which each would be displayed.

Every request is assessed by a conservator before it goes to the loans committee, which meets in February, June and October. — [3] Glass that has been repaired, and anything still on its original wooden base, is rarely approved for travel.

There is no fee for the loan itself. — [4] The borrower pays for packing, transport, courier travel and insurance, all of which we arrange and invoice afterwards.

Enquiries: registrar@halversenglass.example

questions.text: What is the web page mainly about?
choices: An exhibition opening at the museum
A change to the museum's admission charges
The conditions under which the museum lends objects
A vacancy in the registrar's office
questions.explanation: The page sets out who may borrow, when to apply, how requests are assessed and who pays the costs.

questions.text: When must a loan request be submitted?
choices: Nine months after the loans committee meets
As soon as a conservator has assessed the objects
At least nine months before the exhibition opens
questions.explanation: “Requests must reach the registrar at least nine months before the opening date of the exhibition.” February, June and October are the committee's meeting months, not the deadline.

questions.text: What is NOT required in a loan request?
choices: The name of the exhibition's curator
The catalogue numbers of the objects
The dates the objects would be away
A description of the case or mount
questions.explanation: The three items the page asks for are catalogue numbers, the dates away, and the case or mount; nobody is asked to name a curator.

questions.text:
In which of the positions marked [1], [2], [3] and [4] does the following sentence best belong?

“Requests that arrive later than this are held over to the following season.”
questions.explanation: “Later than this” can only refer to the nine-month deadline, so the sentence follows the sentence that sets it. At [4] it would be read as being about the loan fee.

The purchase order number was incorrect.

passages.content:
Kestrel Bay Maritime Museum Reports Record Spring

KESTREL BAY (18 May) — The Kestrel Bay Maritime Museum welcomed 41,600 visitors between February and April, its strongest spring since the building opened in 1998 and an increase of 26 percent on the same period last year.

Director Ingrid Solheim credits the rise to two changes. In January the museum began staying open until 9 P.M. on Fridays, and in March it withdrew its printed guide in favour of a free mobile application offering commentary in six languages.

“The Friday evenings brought us an audience we had never reached — people who are at work all day,” Ms. Solheim said. “The application surprised us more. Nearly half of all visitors now use it.”

The museum will close its east wing on 1 September for eight months while the Whaling Gallery is rebuilt. The remaining galleries, the archive reading room and the café will stay open throughout the work.

The reading room will be closed to visitors.

meta.notes: Complete Reading section in the official shape: Part 5 (30), Part 6 (16, four texts), Part 7 (54: ten single passages, two double, three triple). Numbered 101-200, 75 minutes.

parts.title: Incomplete Sentences
parts.instructions: A word or phrase is missing in each of the sentences below. Four answer choices are given. Select the best answer to complete the sentence.

questions.text: Delegates who register before 15 March will receive a substantial ______ on the conference fee.
questions.explanation: After the article “a” and the adjective “substantial”, a noun is required: “a substantial reduction”.

questions.text: By the time the audit team arrives on Monday, the finance department ______ all supporting invoices.
questions.explanation: “By the time … arrives” sets a deadline in the future, so an action finished before it takes the future perfect “will have compiled”.

questions.text: Passengers may check in online ______ 24 hours of their scheduled departure time.
questions.explanation: “Within 24 hours of” names the period inside which checking in is possible; “during” would need a defined event rather than a countdown.

questions.text: Ms. Adeyemi has been asked to ______ the Lisbon branch at next month's regional banking forum.
questions.explanation: To “represent the branch” is to act on its behalf. “Present” would require something shown to an audience rather than an organisation, and one attends a forum, not a branch.

questions.text: Claims submitted after the 31 May deadline ______ in the following quarter.
questions.explanation: Claims do not act on themselves; the subject receives the action, so the future passive “will be processed” is needed.

questions.text: The maintenance crew worked ______ through the night to restore power to the northern grid.
questions.explanation: An adverb is needed to modify the verb “worked”: “worked steadily through the night”.

questions.text: The turbines will remain offline ______ the replacement gearboxes clear customs.
questions.explanation: “Until” marks the point at which the offline period ends. “Despite” and “in case of” cannot introduce a clause with a finite verb.

questions.text: The agency recommends ______ travel insurance at the time of booking rather than a few days before departure.
questions.explanation: “Recommend” takes a gerund when no object comes between it and the verb: “recommends purchasing”.

questions.text: Applicants must supply ______ proof of address before a business account can be opened.
questions.explanation: An adjective is needed before the noun “proof”: “satisfactory proof of address”.

questions.text: Guests ______ leave luggage at the front desk after checking out, at no additional charge.
questions.explanation: “At no additional charge” describes a service offered to guests, so the permission modal “may” fits; “must” would turn an option into an obligation.

questions.text: The premium is calculated ______ the basis of the driver's claims history over the previous five years.
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is “on the basis of”.

questions.text: Since the tariff changed in January, the utility ______ more than four thousand enquiries about billing.
questions.explanation: “Since January” opens a period that runs up to the present, which takes the present perfect “has received”.

questions.text: The new fare structure is ______ simpler than the one it replaces.
questions.explanation: An adverb is needed to intensify the comparative adjective “simpler”: “considerably simpler”.

questions.text: The emergency generators ______ twice since the substation was upgraded in April.
questions.explanation: “Since April” calls for the present perfect, and the generators undergo the testing rather than carry it out, so the passive “have been tested” is required.

questions.text: Travellers ______ passports expire within six months of arrival may be refused entry.
questions.explanation: A possessive relative is needed to link “travellers” to “passports”: “travellers whose passports expire”. “Who” would leave “passports” without a subject.

questions.text: All branch managers are expected to ______ strictly to the revised lending guidelines.
questions.explanation: Only “adhere” is completed by “to”; “comply” would need “with”, and “observe” and “follow” take a direct object with no preposition.

questions.text: The firm has appointed an external ______ to review its data-protection procedures.
questions.explanation: “An external” must be followed by a noun, and the one appointed to review procedures is a person: “an external adviser”.

questions.text: ______ the storm damaged three substations, service was restored to most customers within a day.
questions.explanation: A conjunction is needed before the clause “the storm damaged three substations”; “despite” and “owing to” must be followed by a noun phrase.

questions.text: When the delegation ______ tomorrow, a representative from the consulate will meet them at the gate.
questions.explanation: A time clause introduced by “when” uses the present simple for future reference; the future is already carried by “will meet”.

questions.text: Very ______ information was available about the cause of the delay when the notice was first posted.
questions.explanation: “Information” is uncountable, so it takes “little”; “few” and “several” count separate items.

questions.text: The bank's mobile application has proved highly ______ with customers under thirty.
questions.explanation: “Prove” is a linking verb here and takes an adjective complement: “has proved highly popular”.

questions.text: The regional operator has agreed ______ the timetable until the track works are finished.
questions.explanation: “Agree” is followed by the infinitive: “has agreed to adjust the timetable”.

questions.text: Delegates travelling ______ rail should keep their tickets for reimbursement.
questions.explanation: A means of transport named without an article takes “by”: “by rail”. “On” would require a specific vehicle, as in “on the 7:15 train”.

questions.text: Policyholders ______ by e-mail as soon as a decision on their claim has been reached.
questions.explanation: The policyholders receive the message rather than send it, so the present passive “are notified” is required.

questions.text: If the ministry ______ the subsidy last year, the wind farm would have opened on schedule.
questions.explanation: The main clause “would have opened” marks an unreal past condition, which requires the past perfect “had approved”.

questions.text: The claims department cleared the backlog with remarkable ______.
questions.explanation: After the preposition “with” and the adjective “remarkable”, only a noun can stand: “with remarkable efficiency”.

questions.text: Contractors ______ wear high-visibility clothing at all times inside the plant.
questions.explanation: A safety rule that applies at all times is an obligation, expressed by “must”; “might” and “could” would reduce it to a possibility.

questions.text: The auditors ______ through the branch records for six hours before they found the discrepancy.
questions.explanation: The work ran up to a point in the past fixed by “before they found”, so the past perfect continuous is needed.

questions.text: Passengers must present a printed or digital boarding ______ before entering the departure lounge.
questions.explanation: The fixed compound is “boarding pass”; a ticket records the purchase of travel rather than the document issued at check-in.

questions.text: ______ in renewable capacity has slowed in the last two quarters, according to the regulator.
questions.explanation: The subject of “has slowed” must be a noun: “Growth in renewable capacity”.

parts.title: Text Completion
parts.instructions: Read the texts that follow. A word, phrase, or sentence is missing in parts of each text. Select the best answer to complete the text.

passages.label: Questions 131-134 refer to the following e-mail.
passages.content:
To: Business Banking Clients
From: Ingrid Halvorsen, Head of Client Operations
Date: 12 October
Subject: Uploading documents to Nordvik Direct

From 1 November, statements and identity documents can be sent to us through Nordvik Direct, our online client portal. Papers posted to the branch will still be {{131}}, but they take up to ten working days to reach our verification team.

Uploading a file takes about a minute. Once a document has arrived, the portal {{132}} its status until the review is complete. {{133}} Most accounts are cleared within two working days.

Please note that scanned pages must be legible; blurred images are returned for resubmission. If you are unsure whether a document meets the standard, our client desk will {{134}} it with you first.

Thank you for banking with Nordvik.

questions.explanation: After “will still be” a past participle is needed, because the posted papers undergo the handling: “will still be processed”.
The singular subject “the portal” needs a finite third-person verb: “the portal displays its status”.

choices: Paper statements will no longer be issued to any client.
The portal is unavailable between midnight and 6 A.M.
You will also receive an e-mail each time a document is approved.
Identity documents must be certified by a solicitor before they are sent.
questions.explanation: The sentence extends the point just made about being kept informed of a document's status, and leads into how quickly accounts are cleared. Requiring certification by a solicitor would contradict a process the e-mail says takes about a minute.
“Review it with you” describes the check the desk offers before a client uploads; “submit” would name the client's own action rather than the desk's help.

passages.label: Questions 135-138 refer to the following policy.
passages.content:
VESTRA ENERGY — PLANNED OUTAGE NOTIFICATION POLICY

Vestra Energy carries out scheduled maintenance on the distribution network throughout the year. {{135}} This policy sets out how and when the households affected are informed.

Written notice is posted to every property on the affected circuit at least fourteen days {{136}} the work begins. The notice states the date, the expected start and finish times, and a reference number for enquiries.

Customers who have registered a mobile number also receive a text message on the previous evening. Registration is free and {{137}} be completed at any time through the customer portal.

If a planned outage is cancelled or moved to another date, a second notice is issued. Where the change is made less than 48 hours in advance, customers are contacted {{138}} by telephone.

choices: Some of this work requires the supply to be switched off for several hours.
Emergency repairs are handled by a separate contractor.
The network was last extended eleven years ago.
Customers may change supplier at any time without penalty.
questions.explanation: It connects the maintenance named before it to the notification rules that follow: an interruption to supply is precisely what households need to be told about. Emergency repairs fall outside a policy on planned outages.
The notice is placed earlier in time than the work, which “before” expresses; “since” and “until” would reverse or stretch that relationship.
Registration is an option, and “can be completed at any time” states that it is available; “must” would make it compulsory, which the paragraph does not.
An adverb is needed to modify the passive verb “are contacted”: “are contacted directly by telephone”.

passages.label: Questions 139-142 refer to the following letter.
passages.content:
Kestrel Travel Management
41 Rue des Ateliers, Brussels

18 February

Ms. Paulina Rzepka
Procurement Manager
Halberd Instruments

Dear Ms. Rzepka,

Thank you for asking us to review your company's travel arrangements for the coming year. Our analysts {{139}} your booking records, and I am pleased to enclose a summary of what they found.

Two figures stand out. First, more than a third of your flights are booked within seven days of departure, {{140}} raises the average fare by roughly €180 per journey. Second, your teams stayed in eleven different hotel chains in Frankfurt alone.

Both figures can be improved without restricting where your staff stay. {{141}}, we would suggest a preferred-hotel list of four properties and an internal booking deadline of fourteen days.

I will telephone you next week to arrange a meeting. {{142}}

Yours sincerely,

Bruno Okonkwo
Client Director

questions.explanation: The review is finished and its summary is enclosed, so the present perfect “have examined” is required; the continuous would suggest the work is still under way.
A relative pronoun referring back to the whole preceding clause is needed: “which raises the average fare”. “It” would leave two main clauses joined by nothing but a comma.
The sentence narrows the general claim before it into two concrete proposals, which “specifically” signals; “nevertheless” would announce a contrast the paragraph does not make.

choices: Please settle the enclosed invoice within thirty days.
If a particular morning suits you better, my assistant can be reached on the number below.
We are unfortunately unable to advise on hotel bookings.
Your account has been transferred to our Warsaw office.
questions.explanation: It follows directly from the offer to telephone and gives Ms. Rzepka a way to fix a time. Declining to advise on hotels would contradict the preferred-hotel list recommended a paragraph earlier.

passages.label: Questions 143-146 refer to the following article.
passages.content:
Coastal Railway Draws Record Summer Traffic

PORTHAVEN — The narrow-gauge line linking Porthaven to the cliff villages of the northern coast carried 214,000 passengers between May and September, its highest figure {{143}} the railway reopened in 2011.

Operators credit a combined ticket, sold together with entry to the maritime museum, for much of the rise. {{144}} It now accounts for nearly a quarter of all summer journeys.

The increase has not pleased everyone. Residents of Aldmere, the smallest village on the route, report that the single car park fills by nine in the morning. The regional tourism board says it is {{145}} the possibility of a shuttle bus from a field outside the village.

A decision is expected before the timetable for next season {{146}} in January.

questions.explanation: “Since” fixes the starting point of the period across which the figure is a record; “until” would place the record before the reopening.

choices: The museum closed for refurbishment in March and has not reopened.
Introduced in April, it costs €18 and covers travel in both directions.
Passenger numbers fell sharply in the two seasons that followed.
The railway employs eleven drivers, three of whom work part time.
questions.explanation: It supplies the details of the combined ticket just mentioned, which the next sentence then quantifies with “It now accounts for…”. A museum closed since March could not be selling entry with the ticket.
“Exploring the possibility” fits an idea still under consideration, as the decision expected in January confirms; “refusing” or “denying” would already have ruled the shuttle out.
The timetable undergoes the publishing, so the passive is needed, and a time clause introduced by “before” uses the present rather than the future.

parts.instructions: In this part you will read a selection of texts. Each text or set of texts is followed by several questions. Select the best answer for each question.

passages.label: Questions 147-148 refer to the following notice.
passages.content:
NOTICE TO ALL TENANTS — Nordvik Business Centre

Saturday 18 April, 06:00-14:00

The server rooms on floor 4 will remain on the backup supply. Tenants who keep equipment anywhere else in the building are asked to shut it down before leaving on Friday 17 April.

Questions: facilities@nordvikcentre.example or extension 4180.

questions.text: What is the purpose of the notice?
choices: To announce a change in the building's opening hours
To introduce a new facilities contractor
To warn tenants of a temporary loss of power
To request payment of an annual maintenance charge
questions.explanation: The notice is headed “Planned electrical maintenance” and states that power will be interrupted for an eight-hour window on 18 April.

questions.text: What are tenants asked to do?
choices: Switch off their equipment before the weekend
Enter the building through the loading bay
Report to the facilities office on 18 April
questions.explanation: Tenants with equipment outside the floor-4 server rooms are told to “shut it down before leaving on Friday 17 April”. The loading bay is mentioned only because it will be locked.

passages.label: Questions 149-150 refer to the following text-message chain.
passages.content:
Aleksandra Wójcik (10:12)
Are you still at the Hallberg office? The audit files we sent on Tuesday have come back to us unsigned.

Daniel Okonjo (10:14)
Just left the car park. I can turn around if it is urgent.

Aleksandra Wójcik (10:15)
Not urgent exactly, but the filing deadline is Friday and Ms. Hallberg travels on Thursday morning.

Daniel Okonjo (10:17)
Then it is urgent. Going back now. Do you need anything else from her, or is it only the signature?

Aleksandra Wójcik (10:19)
Only the signature, on pages 3 and 11. I will e-mail those two pages to their front desk so they can print them for you.

Daniel Okonjo (10:21)
Ask them for two sets. I would like to leave a signed copy with her.

Aleksandra Wójcik (10:22)
Done. I am copying you in as well, in case the desk is unattended when you arrive.

questions.text: What problem does Ms. Wójcik report?
choices: A filing deadline has been brought forward.
An office has closed for the day.
Documents were returned without a signature.
questions.explanation: Her first message says the audit files “have come back to us unsigned”. The Friday deadline is mentioned later as context, not as something that has changed.

questions.text: At 10:17, what does Mr. Okonjo most likely mean when he writes, “Then it is urgent”?
choices: He believes the deadline has already passed.
He realises there is very little time left to obtain the signature.
He thinks Ms. Hallberg should postpone her trip.
He wants Ms. Wójcik to handle the matter instead.
questions.explanation: He replies immediately after learning that Ms. Hallberg travels on Thursday and the deadline is Friday, which leaves almost no window — hence “Going back now”.

passages.label: Questions 151-153 refer to the following press release.
passages.content:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
Vantorp Energi to supply district heating to Kallsund industrial park

VANTORP, 6 May — Vantorp Energi announced today that it has been selected to build and operate a district heating network for the Kallsund industrial park, serving eighteen manufacturing and logistics tenants from the winter of next year.

The network will draw its heat from the aluminium works on the northern edge of the park, which currently discharges cooling water into the harbour at around 70°C. Vantorp Energi estimates that recovering that water will meet roughly 60 percent of the park's annual heating demand and cut the park's gas purchases by €2.4 million a year.

“The heat is already being produced,” said Ingrid Solheim, the company's chief operating officer. “Our contribution is a pipe network and a set of pumps. What makes the project unusual is that eighteen competing tenants agreed to sign a single shared supply contract.”

Construction begins in September. An information evening for park tenants will be held on 28 May at the Kallsund conference centre.

questions.text: Where will the heat for the new network come from?
choices: Water pumped out of the harbour
questions.explanation: The network “will draw its heat from the aluminium works”. The harbour is where that water is currently discharged, not a source.

questions.text: According to Ms. Solheim, what is unusual about the project?
choices: The temperature of the water being recovered
The speed at which construction will be completed
The size of the savings on gas
The tenants' agreement to share one contract
questions.explanation: She says explicitly, “What makes the project unusual is that eighteen competing tenants agreed to sign a single shared supply contract.”

questions.text: In paragraph 3, the word “draw” is closest in meaning to
questions.explanation: “Draw its heat from the aluminium works” means take or obtain it from there. “Attract” would reverse the direction of the transfer.

passages.label: Questions 154-156 refer to the following letter.
passages.content:
Meridian Mutual Insurance
14 Rua das Amoreiras, Lisbon

11 February

Ms. Chiaki Morimoto
Aparthotel Rosa dos Ventos
Setúbal

Yours sincerely,

Bartosz Lewandowski
Renewals Team

questions.text: Why was the letter written?
choices: To request payment of an overdue premium
To respond to a claim for flood damage
To set out the terms of a renewal
To explain why cover has been withdrawn
questions.explanation: The letter states the renewal date, the new premium and the two terms that have changed. No claim has been made and nothing is overdue.

questions.text: What is stated about claims for glass?
choices: The amount the policyholder must pay has increased.
They are no longer covered by the policy.
They must be reported within thirty days.
They carry a separate additional premium.
questions.explanation: “The excess payable on glass claims has risen from €250 to €400” — the excess is the part the policyholder pays.

questions.text: What is suggested about the ground-floor storage rooms?
choices: They are insured under a separate policy.
They will be inspected before 1 April.
They are no longer used for storage.
They are now considered less likely to flood.
questions.explanation: The insurer dropped the flood exclusion only after the drainage works were completed, which implies the flood risk there is now judged lower.

passages.label: Questions 157-159 refer to the following article.
passages.content:
Slow trains, full carriages

Overnight rail travel across the continent, written off a decade ago as a relic, carried 4.1 million passengers last year — the highest figure since 2004. Three operators have added routes in the past eighteen months, and a fourth has ordered sleeping cars for delivery in 2028.

The revival is not driven by price. A berth from Kraków to Trieste costs €149 return, roughly twice the cheapest flight on the same day. Operators say their passengers are buying something else: a night that does not have to be spent in a hotel, and an arrival in the centre of the city that needs no onward transfer.

Load factors tell the story. On the Kraków-Trieste service, single-occupancy cabins sell out first and are typically booked eleven weeks ahead, while the ordinary seated carriages on the same train run at 62 percent.

The constraint is rolling stock. A sleeping car takes four years to build, and only two manufacturers on the continent still make them.

questions.text: What is the article mainly about?
choices: A fall in the cost of air travel
Renewed demand for overnight rail services
The closure of a rolling-stock manufacturer
A hotel chain expanding near railway stations
questions.explanation: The article opens with record passenger numbers on overnight trains and explains why demand has returned. The manufacturers appear only as a limit on supply.

questions.text: According to operators, why do passengers choose overnight trains?
choices: They offer discounts to frequent travellers.
They remove the need to pay for a hotel night.
They run more often than daytime services.
questions.explanation: Passengers are buying “a night that does not have to be spent in a hotel”. The article states directly that the revival is not driven by price.

questions.text: What is indicated about single-occupancy cabins?
choices: They are reserved well in advance.
They cost less than a seat in an ordinary carriage.
They are offered on only two routes.
questions.explanation: They “sell out first and are typically booked eleven weeks ahead”. The 2028 date refers to an order for new sleeping cars, not to the cabins in service today.

passages.label: Questions 160-162 refer to the following online chat discussion.
passages.content:
Priya Ramanathan (09:02)

questions.text: What will happen at 18:00?

A meeting of the three writers will begin.
A system will stop accepting new entries.

Many are unaware of the paper forms held in their branch.
They will be asked to work over the weekend.
They have ordered more cards than usual.

questions.text: What will Ms. Nwosu do next?

Prepare a message for the branch network

passages.label: Questions 163-165 refer to the following e-mail.
