questions.text: Why did Ms. Marstrand write the e-mail?
choices: To advertise a newly created tour
To explain a change to a booked itinerary
To request payment of an outstanding balance
questions.explanation: The subject line reads “Change to your 3 November departure”, and the e-mail sets out how day four has been rebuilt after the ferry was withdrawn.

questions.text: What is indicated about the new day-four arrangement?
choices: It takes longer than the original plan.
It requires an extra night in a hotel.
It will be led by a different guide.
It ends with an earlier return flight.
questions.explanation: “The drive adds ninety minutes to the day.” The e-mail states that the hotel, guide and return flight are unchanged.

questions.text: What is Mr. Bergström asked to do?
choices: Apply in writing for the refund
Pay a fee for changing the itinerary
questions.explanation: “Please confirm by 20 October that the revised day four is acceptable.” The refund is automatic and no fee is charged.

passages.label: Questions 166-169 refer to the following web page.
passages.content:
www.halvorsen-adeyemi.example/about

About Halvorsen & Adeyemi

Halvorsen & Adeyemi advises industrial clients on energy procurement and metering. — [1] — The firm began in 2009 as a two-person practice above a bakery in Trondheim, with a single client: a fish-processing plant that could not explain its own electricity bill.

We now employ forty-one people across three offices and audit roughly €90 million of annual energy spend on behalf of our clients. — [2] — Our work is deliberately narrow. We do not sell equipment, we do not install anything, and we take no commission from suppliers. Our only revenue is the fee our clients pay us.

That independence occasionally costs us work. — [3] — A client who wants one firm to audit, specify and install is better served elsewhere, and we say so at the first meeting.

Every engagement begins with a fortnight of meter data and one uncomfortable question: what are you paying for that you are not using? On average, the answer is eleven percent of the bill. — [4] —

Offices: Trondheim · Gdańsk · Lagos

questions.text: How did Halvorsen & Adeyemi begin?
choices: As a division of a larger consultancy
With offices in three cities at once
By installing metering equipment for suppliers
As a small practice serving one client
questions.explanation: It “began in 2009 as a two-person practice above a bakery in Trondheim, with a single client”. The three offices came later.

questions.text: How does the firm earn its income?
choices: From commissions paid by energy suppliers
From the sale of metering equipment
From fees charged to the clients it advises
From installation contracts on industrial sites
questions.explanation: “Our only revenue is the fee our clients pay us.” The page rules out commission, equipment sales and installation explicitly.

questions.text: What information about the firm is NOT given on the web page?
choices: The professional qualifications of its consultants
The year in which it was founded
The number of people it employs
The cities in which it has offices
questions.explanation: The page gives 2009, forty-one employees and the three office cities, but says nothing about what qualifications its consultants hold.

questions.text:
In which of the positions marked [1], [2], [3] and [4] does the following sentence best belong?

“For a plant spending €4 million a year on power, that is €440,000 left on the table.”
questions.explanation: The sentence converts the eleven percent into euros, so it can only follow the sentence that supplies that figure, at [4].

passages.label: Questions 170-171 refer to the following memo.
passages.content:
MEMORANDUM

To: All holders of a corporate card
From: Renata Duarte, Head of Finance
Date: 22 January
Subject: New card provider from 1 March

Our corporate card programme moves to a new provider on 1 March. Your current card will stop working at midnight on 28 February; please destroy it rather than returning it to this office.

Replacement cards will be posted to your home address during the week of 16 February and will arrive unactivated. Activate yours by calling the number on the sticker, from the telephone number we hold for you in the staff directory. If that number is out of date, correct your entry before 9 February.

Claims for January and February must be submitted under the old system by 5 March. Anything submitted after that date has to be re-entered by hand, which delays reimbursement by about three weeks.

Spending limits and approval routes are unchanged.

questions.text: What should staff do with their current cards?
choices: Return them to the finance office
Post them to the new provider
questions.explanation: “Please destroy it rather than returning it to this office.” The 5 March date applies to expense claims, not to the cards.

questions.text: What is suggested about staff whose directory entry is out of date?
choices: They will not be sent a replacement card.
They must collect their card in person.
They may be unable to activate their new card.
Their spending limit will be reduced.
questions.explanation: Activation must be done from the number held in the directory, so an incorrect entry would block it — which is why corrections are due by 9 February.

passages.label: Questions 172-175 refer to the following policy.
passages.content:
KESTREL HOUSE HOTELS — Cancellation and amendment policy
Applies to all direct bookings made on or after 1 June

Flexible rate
Cancel or amend free of charge up to 18:00 on the day before arrival. After that time, one night is charged.

Saver rate
Non-refundable; the full stay is charged at the time of booking. Dates may be moved once, to any date within six months, for a fee of €25 per room.

Group bookings (five rooms or more)
Cancel up to 21 days before arrival at no cost. Between 20 and 8 days before arrival, half the value of the booking is charged. Within 7 days, the full value is charged. The number of rooms may be reduced by up to 20 percent at any time before the 21-day point without penalty.

Amendments must be made through the hotel holding the booking, not through central reservations. Bookings made through a travel agent or an online platform are governed by that partner's terms rather than by this policy.

Guests who do not arrive and have not cancelled are charged under the rules of their rate.

questions.text: By when must a flexible-rate booking be cancelled to avoid a charge?
choices: By 18:00 on the day before arrival
By 18:00 on the day of arrival
questions.explanation: The flexible rate allows free cancellation “up to 18:00 on the day before arrival”; after that one night is charged. The seven- and twenty-one-day limits belong to group bookings.

questions.text: What is possible with a saver-rate booking?
choices: A full refund within twenty-four hours
A transfer to a different hotel at no cost
Cancellation up to eight days before arrival
One change of dates in return for a fee
questions.explanation: The saver rate is non-refundable, but “dates may be moved once, to any date within six months, for a fee of €25 per room”.

questions.text: A group booking of ten rooms is cancelled twelve days before arrival. What will be charged?
choices: Half the value of the booking
The full value of the booking
questions.explanation: Twelve days falls inside the 20-to-8-day band, for which “half the value of the booking is charged”. The full value applies only within seven days.

questions.text: What is suggested about a reservation made through an online platform?
choices: It cannot be amended at any point.
It qualifies for a reduction of 20 percent.
The terms above do not apply to it.
It must be confirmed twenty-one days in advance.
questions.explanation: Such bookings “are governed by that partner's terms rather than by this policy”, so the rates and deadlines set out here do not cover them.

passages.content:
To: facilities@rivergatepark.example
From: p.oyelaran@sundermeyer-actuarial.example
Date: 18 February
Subject: Generator hire — Building C

Dear site office,

Thank you for the notice. Sundermeyer Actuarial occupies the third and fourth floors of Building C, and the day you have given us is the last day of our quarterly reporting cycle. Our analysts cannot lose it, so I would like to book a portable generator.

Please confirm that the fee covers the whole building, as the wording suggests. The recruitment agency on our ground floor would also like to keep working and would share the cost with us.

Two further points. Our server room is cooled by a unit that draws far more power than ordinary office equipment, and I need to know whether the generator will support it. And since our staff will be on site all day, could you confirm that the stairwell doors will unlock from the inside while the entry system is running on battery?

I am writing well inside your deadline, but tell me at once if anything further is needed.

Kind regards,

Paulo Oyelaran
Operations Manager

questions.text: What is the purpose of the notice?
choices: To announce a change to the tenancy agreement
To warn tenants that electricity will be cut off for a day
To advertise portable generators for sale
To explain a rise in service charges
questions.explanation: The notice gives the day on which each building will lose mains electricity while the substations are replaced. Generators are offered for hire, not for sale.

questions.text: On what date will Mr. Oyelaran's firm lose its electricity supply?
questions.explanation: The e-mail places Sundermeyer Actuarial in Building C, and the notice gives Building C the Thursday 5 March slot.

questions.text: Why does Mr. Oyelaran mention the recruitment agency?
choices: To explain that another tenant would share the cost of the generator
To pass on a complaint made by another tenant
To ask that the agency be moved to a different building
To identify who will pay the whole hire fee
questions.explanation: He asks whether the €340 covers the whole building because the ground-floor agency “would share the cost with us”. He never says the agency will pay all of it.

questions.text: Which of Mr. Oyelaran's concerns is NOT addressed in the notice?
choices: The date of the interruption in his building
The cost of hiring a generator
The deadline for requesting a generator
Whether a generator can run a cooling unit
questions.explanation: The notice supplies the dates, the €340 charge and the ten-working-day deadline, but says nothing about how much equipment a generator will support.

questions.text: What does the notice indicate about compensation?
choices: It is paid only to tenants who hire a generator.
It is not available for interruptions of this kind.
It is calculated according to the number of floors occupied.
It must be claimed within ten working days.
questions.explanation: “our standard tenancy agreement does not provide compensation for planned interruptions of this kind”. The ten-working-day limit belongs to generator requests, not to claims.

passages.label: Questions 181-185 refer to the following article and letter to the editor.
passages.content:
Visitor levy to fund coastal path
By Ingrid Sælen, 12 May

Kaldvik will introduce a visitor levy of €2.50 per guest per night from 1 October, the town council confirmed on Tuesday. The charge will apply to hotels, guesthouses and licensed short-term rentals, and will be collected by the operator and passed to the council each quarter.

Officials expect the levy to raise about €1.4 million in its first full year. Roughly two-thirds is earmarked for the long-delayed coastal path between the harbour and Storneset, with the remainder going to public toilets, waste collection and the summer shuttle bus.

Guests staying more than fourteen consecutive nights will be exempt from the fifteenth night onwards, as will anyone travelling for medical treatment.

Kaldvik recorded 310,000 overnight stays last year, 18 percent more than five years ago. Councillor Renata Bielawska, who chairs the tourism committee, said the town had “reached the point where visitors must contribute to the infrastructure they use”.

A consultation on the collection procedure closes on 30 June.

passages.label: Questions 181-185 refer to the following article and letter to the editor.
passages.content:
To the editor,

I have run a nine-room guesthouse in Kaldvik for twenty-two years, and I am not against the levy in principle. The path your article describes has been promised since before I opened, and the state of the harbour toilets is no advertisement for us. If €2.50 a night buys those things, my guests will pay it without complaint.

My objection is to who does the collecting. Under this scheme I become an unpaid tax collector: I must add the charge, decide who is exempt, hold the money and file a return four times a year. A hotel with a finance office can absorb that. I cannot, and neither can the eleven other small operators I have spoken to.

There is an obvious alternative. The council already licenses every operator in the town. Bill the levy once a year, based on the previous year's declared occupancy, and send us a single invoice. The council collects the same money and I get my evenings back.

I would urge the committee to look at this before the consultation closes.

Halldór Jónsson
Sjøhuset Guesthouse

questions.text: What is the article mainly about?
choices: The completion of a path along the coast
A decline in visitor numbers in Kaldvik
A new charge on overnight visitors
A dispute between hotels and guesthouses
questions.explanation: The article reports the council's decision to introduce a €2.50 nightly visitor levy from 1 October. The coastal path is what the money will pay for; it has not been built.

questions.text: According to the article, how will most of the money raised be spent?
choices: On building a path along the coast
On running the summer shuttle bus
questions.explanation: “Roughly two-thirds is earmarked for the long-delayed coastal path”; the shuttle bus and waste collection share what is left.

questions.text: Who will stop paying the levy part-way through a stay?
choices: Guests staying longer than two weeks
questions.explanation: Guests staying more than fourteen consecutive nights are exempt “from the fifteenth night onwards”. Those travelling for medical treatment are exempt for the whole stay, not part of it.

questions.text: What is Mr. Jónsson's main objection to the levy?
choices: The nightly amount is too high for his guests.
Small operators would have to administer it.
The coastal path is not worth building.
Hotels would be exempt from paying it.
questions.explanation: “My objection is to who does the collecting” — adding the charge, judging exemptions and filing quarterly returns falls on operators too small to absorb the work. He states plainly that his guests will pay the €2.50 without complaint.

questions.text: By what date does Mr. Jónsson want the committee to consider his proposal?
choices: The end of the first quarter
questions.explanation: He asks the committee to look at his alternative “before the consultation closes”, and the article dates that closing at 30 June.

To introduce a new billing system

meta.notes: Complete Reading section in the official shape: Part 5 (30), Part 6 (16, four texts), Part 7 (54: ten single passages, two double, three triple). Numbered 101-200, 75 minutes.

parts.title: Incomplete Sentences
parts.instructions: A word or phrase is missing in each of the sentences below. Four answer choices are given. Select the best answer to complete the sentence.

questions.text: Ravensholm Tooling reported a significant ______ in output after the second assembly line came online.
questions.explanation: After the article “a” and the adjective “significant”, a noun is required: “a significant increase in output”.

questions.text: By the time the safety audit begins next month, the plant ______ all of the recommended guard rails.
questions.explanation: “By the time … next month” sets a deadline in the future, so the future perfect is needed. The present perfect “has installed” cannot reach forward to a future point.

questions.text: The tenants association objected ______ the proposed increase in the monthly maintenance charge.
questions.explanation: The verb “object” takes “to”: “objected to the proposed increase”. “Against” belongs with “protest” or “argue”, not with “object”.

questions.text: Because the sensor readings had drifted out of tolerance, the technician had to ______ the machine before the next production run.
questions.explanation: Readings that have drifted out of tolerance are corrected by adjusting the instrument, which is exactly what “recalibrate” means. Reinforcing or moving the machine would leave the readings wrong.

questions.text: The property manager praised the maintenance crew for responding so ______ to the flooding in the basement.
questions.explanation: The blank modifies the verb “responding”, so an adverb is required: “responding so quickly”.

questions.text: ______ the zoning application was submitted on time, the council will not rule on it before October.
questions.explanation: Only “although” can introduce a full clause with its own subject and verb; “despite”, “in spite of” and “owing to” must be followed by a noun phrase.

questions.text: The apprentices ______ portfolios were submitted after the deadline will be assessed in the next cycle.
questions.explanation: The portfolios belong to the apprentices, so the possessive relative “whose” is needed; “who” would leave “portfolios” with no link to their owners.

questions.text: The vacant retail unit on Kellerman Street ______ into two smaller offices next spring.
questions.explanation: The unit does not perform the action, it receives it, so the future passive “will be divided” is required.

questions.text: Ms. Adeyemi's report on the conveyor failure was unusually ______, running to fewer than two pages.
questions.explanation: After the linking verb “was” and the adverb “unusually”, an adjective completes the sentence: “was unusually concise”.

questions.text: The new hydraulic press runs far ______ than the model it replaced, which has reduced complaints from the neighbouring units.
questions.explanation: “Than” signals a comparison, so the adverb modifying “runs” must take the comparative form “more quietly”.

questions.text: Hollandale Engineering ______ apprenticeships in precision machining since the plant opened in 1998.
questions.explanation: “Since 1998” connects a starting point in the past to the present, which calls for the present perfect “has offered”.

questions.text: The surveyor's fee is payable ______ receipt of the completed valuation report.
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is “payable on receipt of”, meaning as soon as the report arrives.

questions.text: Several tenants have complained about the ______ of the lift in the north tower.
questions.explanation: The object of the preposition “about” must be a noun phrase: “the reliability of the lift”.

questions.text: The apprenticeship board recommends ______ a logbook of every task completed on the shop floor.
questions.explanation: “Recommend” is followed by a gerund when no object comes between: “recommends keeping a logbook”.

questions.text: Demand for warehouse space near the port has ______ sharply since the rail terminal opened.
questions.explanation: “Rise” is intransitive, so demand itself “has risen”. “Raised” would need an object, and “arisen” is used of questions or problems coming into existence.

questions.text: The list of approved subcontractors ______ reviewed by the procurement team every quarter.
questions.explanation: The subject is the singular “list”, not the plural “subcontractors” inside the prepositional phrase, so the singular “is” is correct.

questions.text: Vessikko Precision has appointed an external ______ to review its quality management system.
questions.explanation: A person is appointed, not a procedure: “an external auditor to review the system”. “Audit” names the review itself and cannot be given an appointment.

questions.text: Enrolment for the autumn term ______ next Monday and closes on 30 September.
questions.explanation: A fixed point on a published timetable takes the present simple, matching “closes” later in the sentence: “opens next Monday”.

questions.text: The engineer ______ designed the new extraction system will lead Thursday's training session.
questions.explanation: The relative pronoun is the subject of “designed” and refers to a person, so “who” is required; “whom” can only serve as an object.

questions.text: Delegates left the seminar on the revised building regulations feeling thoroughly ______.
questions.explanation: The delegates experience the feeling, so the past participle “confused” is used; “confusing” would describe the seminar rather than the people at it.

questions.text: Board members praised the site team's ______ of the shutdown, which finished a full day early.
questions.explanation: After the possessive “the site team's”, a noun is needed: “the site team's management of the shutdown”.

questions.text: The refurbishment of the north wing is scheduled to finish ______ the end of the second quarter.
questions.explanation: “By” marks the deadline before which the work will be complete. “Until” would describe a period continuing up to that point, which does not fit a verb such as “finish”.

questions.text: Neither the ventilation upgrade ______ the lighting replacement was included in the original budget.
questions.explanation: “Neither” is paired with “nor”: “neither the ventilation upgrade nor the lighting replacement”.

questions.text: Of the three sites shortlisted for the depot, the one beside the motorway offers ______ access for heavy vehicles.
questions.explanation: Three sites are being compared, so the superlative is required; “the better” would be used only of two.

questions.text: Attendance at the evening courses has shown a ______ improvement since the campus shuttle was introduced.
questions.explanation: The blank modifies the noun “improvement”, so an adjective is needed: “a noticeable improvement”. The adverb “noticeably” could only modify a verb or an adjective.

questions.text: Tenants who wish to renew early should submit the form ______ rather than send it through the letting agent.
questions.explanation: The emphatic reflexive “themselves” stresses that the tenants act without help; the object pronoun “them” would have to refer to somebody other than the subject.

questions.text: The quality team ______ the packing line when the power to the building failed.
questions.explanation: The past continuous describes the activity already under way when the sudden event interrupted it: “was inspecting … when the power failed”.

questions.text: A shortage of qualified fitters is the main ______ to expanding the night shift.
questions.explanation: Something standing in the way of a plan is an “obstacle to” it. A shortage of staff is a condition, not an attitude, so it can be neither a refusal nor a reluctance.

questions.text: Only qualified electricians may ______ the distribution boards in the plant room.
questions.explanation: After the modal “may”, the base form of the verb is required: “may access the distribution boards”.

questions.text: The vacant plot behind the depot ______ used for staff parking since the lease was renegotiated.
questions.explanation: The plot receives the action, and “since” runs the situation from a past point up to now, so the present perfect passive “has been used” is required.

passages.label: Questions 131-134 refer to the following notice.
passages.content:
NOTICE TO RESIDENTS
Lift modernisation — Marden Court, north tower

Work to replace the building's two passenger lifts will begin on Monday 6 April and is {{131}} to take eleven weeks.

Throughout the programme only one lift will be in service at any time, so waiting times will be longer than usual. Residents are asked to allow extra time {{132}} the morning rush, particularly between 8 A.M. and 9 A.M.

The goods lift will remain available for deliveries and house moves, but it must be booked at the concierge desk at least twenty-four hours ahead. {{133}} Bookings are taken between 7 A.M. and 7 P.M., seven days a week.

We recognise that the disruption is considerable. The new cars will be quieter, faster and step-free at every landing, and by the end of June both lifts {{134}} back in service. The service charge will not increase as a result of the work.

Kestrel Property Services

questions.explanation: “Is expected to take” is a passive built on the past participle; the active “expects” would make the building work do the expecting.
The blank is followed by the noun phrase “the morning rush”, so the preposition “during” is needed; “while” would require a clause with its own verb.

choices: Large items may be carried in the passenger lift instead.
The concierge desk will be closed for the duration of the programme.
Both passenger lifts will run normally at weekends.
Requests made on the day of a move cannot normally be accommodated.
questions.explanation: The sentence before it sets a twenty-four-hour booking rule, so what follows naturally states the consequence of giving no notice. A closed concierge desk would contradict the booking hours given in the next sentence.
“By the end of June” points to a date still ahead, so the future “will be” is required; “have been” would place the return to service in the past.

passages.label: Questions 135-138 refer to the following e-mail.
passages.content:
To: Production supervisors
From: Dilnoza Karimova, Learning and Development
Date: 12 February
Subject: Places on the March safety-leadership course

Eight places on the two-day safety-leadership course have been reserved for our site, and every place must be filled by 26 February. {{135}} Nominations should therefore reach me by the end of next week.

The course is run at the Ferrow Institute and {{136}} both classroom sessions and a supervised walk-round of a working plant. Anyone who finishes it receives a certificate recognised across the sector.

Travel and accommodation are arranged centrally, so please do not book tickets yourself. Supervisors are reminded {{137}} their team rotas before putting a name forward, as the two days are consecutive.

If more than eight names come in, priority {{138}} to supervisors who have not attended external training in the past two years. The $640 fee is met by the departmental budget.

choices: The course has been postponed until the autumn.
The institute needs a fortnight's notice to confirm each name.
Places are allocated on the day by the course tutors.
The fee has not yet been agreed with the provider.
questions.explanation: “Therefore” shows that this sentence supplies the reason for an internal deadline earlier than the institute's, and only the fortnight of notice does that. The fee is stated at the end of the message, so it cannot still be unsettled.
The verb shares the singular subject “The course” and balances “is run”, so the third-person form “includes” is needed.
“Remind” is followed by an infinitive of purpose: “supervisors are reminded to check their team rotas”.
Priority is something granted rather than something that acts, so the future passive “will be given” fits the conditional clause about extra names.

passages.label: Questions 139-142 refer to the following press release.
passages.content:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

Talvern Drivetrain opens rebuilt foundry in Gliwice

GLIWICE, 3 May — Talvern Drivetrain today opened its rebuilt light-alloy foundry in Gliwice, eighteen months after production was transferred to a temporary site so that the original works could be demolished. The new plant is {{139}} larger than the one it replaces and will employ 210 people, forty more than before.

The rebuild cost $46 million and puts two electric melting furnaces in place of the gas units used previously. Talvern says the change will cut energy consumption per tonne by roughly a third {{140}} shortening the time needed to switch between alloys.

“We could have rebuilt what we had,” said plant director Sunniva Aarø. “We chose instead to design a foundry {{141}} will still be competitive in ten years' time.”

Output will build up over the summer, with full production expected in September. {{142}}

questions.explanation: A comparative adjective is intensified by an adverb such as “considerably”: “considerably larger than”. “Very” cannot modify “larger”, and “much more” cannot precede a comparative — with “large” the intensified comparative is “much larger”.
The two effects happen together, and “while” introduces the second one as a simultaneous gain. “Despite” would set the two in opposition, and “so that” cannot be followed by an -ing form.
The relative pronoun is the subject of “will still be competitive” and refers to the thing “foundry”, so “that” is used; “what” cannot follow the noun it describes.

choices: Journalists may arrange a site visit through the company's press office.
The gas furnaces will be returned to service once demand recovers.
Recruitment for the forty additional posts has been suspended.
Talvern has not yet decided where the new foundry will be built.
questions.explanation: With the production timetable given, the release closes in the standard way, by telling reporters how to visit. Each of the other sentences contradicts the article: the gas units were replaced, forty posts are being added, and the foundry has already opened.

passages.label: Questions 143-146 refer to the following memo.
passages.content:
MEMORANDUM

To: All staff, Alderway House
From: Facilities Management
Date: 19 October
Subject: Move to Unit 7, Ashgrove Park

Our lease on Alderway House ends on 31 January and will not be renewed. From 3 February we will occupy the ground floor of Unit 7, Ashgrove Park, which gives us 1,400 square metres on a single level. For the first time {{143}} of the four departments will have a meeting room of its own.

{{144}} A shuttle bus will run from the station to the park every fifteen minutes between 7:30 A.M. and 9:30 A.M., and again from 4:30 P.M.

Crates will be delivered to each floor in the third week of January. Personal items left in the building after the final Friday {{145}} be recovered, since the keys are handed to the landlord the following morning.

Floor plans are on the intranet. Please send seating requests to me by 15 November so that they can be taken into account {{146}} the layout is fixed.

questions.explanation: “Each of the four departments” takes the singular possessive “its own”; “all” would require “their own”, “both” refers to two, and “every” cannot be followed by “of”.

choices: Parking at Alderway House will be reserved for visitors from November.
The new site is further from the station, and we know this worries many of you.
Ashgrove Park is served by three underground lines and a tram.
Staff who prefer to stay at Alderway House may apply to do so.
questions.explanation: The sentence that follows announces a shuttle from the station, so what comes before it must raise the travel problem the shuttle solves. Staying at Alderway House is impossible once the lease ends.
The clause after “since” explains that the keys are gone, so retrieval is impossible rather than forbidden: “cannot be recovered”.
Requests are useful only while the plan can still change, so “before the layout is fixed” is the deadline meant. “In advance of” and “during” cannot take the clause that follows.

parts.title: Reading Comprehension
parts.instructions: In this part you will read a selection of texts. Each text or set of texts is followed by several questions. Select the best answer for each question.

passages.label: Questions 147-148 refer to the following memo.
passages.content:
MEMORANDUM

To: All production supervisors
From: Ingrid Halvorsen, Plant Operations Manager
Date: 12 March
Subject: Calibration of line 4

The optical inspection unit on line 4 will be recalibrated on Thursday 19 March. Engineers from Kesselring Systems arrive at 6:00 A.M. and expect the work to take about seven hours, so line 4 will not run that day.

Please move your Thursday output targets for line 4 to Friday and Saturday. Overtime for Saturday has been approved; send me the names by Monday 16 March so that the canteen can be staffed.

Line 3 keeps its normal schedule. However, the calibration rig draws on the same compressed-air supply, so line 3 operators may notice slightly slower tool cycling between 9:00 A.M. and noon.

Supervisors do not need to be present for the calibration itself, but I will need one person from each shift to sign off the first inspection run on Friday morning.

questions.text: Why was the memo written?
choices: To introduce a new inspection procedure
To inform supervisors that a line will be out of service
To report the results of a recent calibration
To announce a permanent change to shift hours
questions.explanation: The memo exists to tell supervisors that “line 4 will not run that day” and to have them move their targets accordingly. The calibration is the cause of the shutdown, not a procedure the supervisors are being taught.

questions.text: What is suggested about the compressed-air supply?
choices: It will be replaced during the calibration.
It is monitored by the visiting engineers.
It cannot fully serve two demands at once.
questions.explanation: Line 3 tools are expected to cycle more slowly precisely while the calibration rig is drawing on the same supply, which implies its capacity is stretched. Nothing indicates the supply itself is being changed or watched by the contractor.

passages.label: Questions 149-150 refer to the following online chat discussion.
passages.content:
Petra Wojcik (10:14 A.M.)
The tenants in 6B have reported that the balcony door will not lock. Is there anyone on the approved list who could come today?

Daniel Okonkwo (10:16 A.M.)
Vale Hardware usually can, but they charge a call-out fee for anything booked after 11:00. Shall I ring them now?

Petra Wojcik (10:18 A.M.)
Please do. It is a ground-floor unit, so I would rather not leave it open overnight.

Daniel Okonkwo (10:23 A.M.)
Booked for 12:40. The fee applied, but they waived it because we have three buildings on their contract.

Petra Wojcik (10:25 A.M.)
That is the third balcony door in that block this year. Let us have the whole row looked at before the winter.

Daniel Okonkwo (10:26 A.M.)
I will ask them to quote for it while they are on site.

questions.text: Why does Ms. Wojcik want the repair carried out the same day?
choices: The unit can be reached from the street.
The tenants are moving out tomorrow.
An inspection of the block is due.
questions.explanation: She links the urgency to the flat being on the ground floor and to not wanting it left open overnight, which points to the risk of entry from outside. The fee is Mr. Okonkwo's concern, not hers.

questions.text: At 10:26 A.M., what does Mr. Okonkwo most likely mean when he writes, “I will ask them to quote for it while they are on site”?
choices: He will negotiate a lower call-out fee.
He will ask the tenants to approve the cost.
He will obtain a price for checking the other doors.
He will arrange a second visit for the winter.
questions.explanation: “It” refers back to Ms. Wojcik's request to have the whole row of balcony doors looked at, so he means a price for that wider job. The call-out fee has already been waived.

passages.label: Questions 151-153 refer to the following advertisement.
passages.content:
ASHGROVE TECHNICAL INSTITUTE

Six courses, all taught on our Riverside campus between 6:00 P.M. and 9:00 P.M.

questions.text: Which course runs for the greatest number of weeks?

choices: They are billed once the course has finished.
They are exempt from the final examination.

questions.text: Who may attend the Saturday laboratory sessions without paying?

passages.label: Questions 154-156 refer to the following e-mail.
passages.content:
To: Beatriz Salgado <b.salgado@northfieldlabs.example>
From: Karolina Brzezinska <k.brzezinska@harborstone.example>
Date: 3 October
Subject: Lift modernisation — Fenwick Court

Dear Ms. Salgado,

Both passenger lifts at Fenwick Court are original to the 1978 building and have become steadily more expensive to maintain. The owners have now released funds to replace the drive systems and controllers in both cars.

Work begins on 2 November and will run for roughly nine weeks. The contractor takes one lift out of service at a time, so a single car stays available throughout. During the changeover week of 21 December, however, both cars will be down for four days.

Because your laboratory occupies the fifth and sixth floors, this will be more disruptive for you than for our ground-floor tenants. If you would like to bring deliveries of heavy equipment forward, the goods entrance on Marlow Lane can be reserved for your exclusive use on any weekday in October at no cost.

Please let me know by 17 October whether you wish to book it.

Kind regards,

Karolina Brzezinska
Building Manager, Harborstone Property Services

questions.text: What is one purpose of the e-mail?
choices: To announce an increase in service charges
To confirm that a lease has been renewed
To offer the use of a facility at no charge
To request payment for completed repairs
questions.explanation: Alongside the notice of the works, Ms. Brzezinska offers exclusive use of the Marlow Lane goods entrance “at no cost” and asks for a decision by 17 October.

questions.text: How long will the building be left with no working lift?
questions.explanation: One car remains in service throughout except during the changeover week, when “both cars will be down for four days”. Nine weeks is the length of the whole project.

questions.text: In paragraph 1, the word “released” is closest in meaning to
questions.explanation: The owners have put money at the manager's disposal for the work, so “released funds” means the funds have been made available. “Published” fits a different sense of the verb, used of announcements rather than money.

passages.label: Questions 157-159 refer to the following article.
passages.content:
Small Manufacturers Share the Cost of Testing

RIVERTON (14 May) — Nineteen precision-parts makers in the Riverton industrial district have formed a cooperative to buy testing equipment that none of them could justify on its own.

The group's first purchase, a computed-tomography scanner installed in a leased unit on Kilner Road, allows a finished component to be inspected internally without being cut open. [1] Members book time on the machine through a shared calendar and are billed by the hour.

“We were each sending parts to a laboratory two hundred kilometres away and waiting nine days for a report,” said Adaeze Nwachukwu, who runs a twelve-person machine shop and chairs the cooperative. “Now it is the same afternoon.” [2]

Membership costs $4,000 a year plus usage fees. [3] The cooperative estimates that a member sending forty components a year for inspection recovers the subscription within seven months.

[4] A second unit, for surface-roughness measurement, is expected before the end of the year, and the group has opened discussions with the technical institute about using the scanner for student projects two evenings a week.

questions.text: What is the article mainly about?
choices: A shared arrangement that gives small firms access to equipment
A merger of nineteen manufacturing companies
A testing laboratory that has opened a second branch
A training partnership between industry and a college
questions.explanation: The whole piece describes a cooperative formed so that member firms can use a scanner none of them could buy alone. The talks with the technical institute are one late detail, not the subject.

questions.text: According to Ms. Nwachukwu, what has changed for her business?
choices: The price charged by the outside laboratory
The number of components it produces
The time needed to obtain test results
questions.explanation: She contrasts waiting nine days for a report with getting one “the same afternoon”. She mentions the size of her shop only to identify herself, and says nothing about its output or about laboratory prices.

questions.text:
In which of the positions marked [1], [2], [3] and [4] does the following sentence best belong?

“Its ambitions do not stop with the scanner.”
questions.explanation: The sentence introduces further plans, and only at [4] is it followed by them: a second measuring unit and talks with the technical institute. At [3] it would interrupt the run of figures about membership cost and payback.

passages.label: Questions 160-162 refer to the following text-message chain.
passages.content:
Tobias Lindqvist (8:02 A.M.)
The crane operator reads 14 metres per second on the mast anemometer. Our limit for lifting the roof panels is 12.

Rosa Mendieta (8:04 A.M.)
Then the panels do not go up today. What else can the team get on with?

Tobias Lindqvist (8:06 A.M.)
Ground-floor blockwork, or they can start setting out the plant room. Neither needs the crane.

Rosa Mendieta (8:07 A.M.)
Set out the plant room. The blockwork gang is not on site until Wednesday and I would rather not have two trades in the same bay.

Tobias Lindqvist (8:09 A.M.)
Understood. One thing — the plant-room drawings in the site office are revision C. Friday's e-mail mentioned a revision D.

Rosa Mendieta (8:12 A.M.)
Do not touch anything until I send it. Give me ten minutes.

Tobias Lindqvist (8:13 A.M.)
Will do. I will have them clear the delivery bay in the meantime.

questions.text: Why will the roof panels not be installed?
choices: Conditions on site exceed a safety limit.
The panels have not been delivered.
Another trade is working in the same bay.
questions.explanation: The wind reads 14 metres per second against a lifting limit of 12. The blockwork gang is not on site at all, so no other trade is in the way.

questions.text: At 8:12 A.M., what does Ms. Mendieta most likely mean when she writes, “Do not touch anything until I send it”?
choices: She wants the crane shut down for the day.
She intends to come to the site herself.
She has not yet decided where the plant room goes.
Work should wait for the current version of the drawings.
questions.explanation: “It” is the revision D drawing Mr. Lindqvist has just said the site office is missing, so she is holding the work until the up-to-date sheet arrives. The crane is already standing idle for another reason.

questions.text: What does Ms. Mendieta indicate about the blockwork gang?
choices: It will not arrive until later in the week.
It has completed its part of the job.
It is working from an outdated drawing.
It needs the crane to continue.
questions.explanation: “The blockwork gang is not on site until Wednesday” is her reason for choosing the plant room instead. The drawing problem concerns the plant room, not the blockwork.

passages.label: Questions 163-165 refer to the following notice.
passages.content:
NOTICE TO ALL OCCUPIERS — Wharfedale Business Park
Resurfacing of the north car park

The north car park will be resurfaced between Monday 6 April and Friday 17 April. For those two weeks it is closed completely, including the loading bays behind Units 9 to 14.

Alternative arrangements

Staff parking: the overflow area on Tannery Lane opens at 6:30 A.M. Permits are not required, but please display your unit number on the dashboard.

Deliveries: use the south gate. The barrier is staffed from 7:00 A.M. to 6:00 P.M. Vehicles over 7.5 tonnes must book a slot with the estate office at least one working day ahead.

Waste collection: bins move to the paved area beside Unit 3 for the duration of the work.

The cycle racks are unaffected.

The contractor works until 8:00 P.M. on weekdays and does not work at weekends. Noise will be heaviest during the first three days, when the existing surface is broken out.

Questions and complaints: estate office, extension 214.

questions.text: According to the notice, what is NOT required of drivers during the work?
choices: Booking ahead for a heavy vehicle
Entering by the south gate to deliver
Holding a permit to park on Tannery Lane
Showing a unit number on the dashboard
questions.explanation: The notice states plainly that permits are not required for the overflow area, although a unit number must still be displayed. Booking and the south gate are both stated requirements.

questions.text: When is the work expected to be at its noisiest?
choices: At the start of the closure
questions.explanation: “Noise will be heaviest during the first three days”, when the old surface is broken out. No work at all takes place at weekends.

questions.text: What is suggested about the businesses in Units 9 to 14?
choices: They will have to take deliveries elsewhere in April.
They will lose access to their premises.
They must move their own waste bins.
They are excused from the parking arrangements.
questions.explanation: Their loading bays are inside the closed area, so for those two weeks their goods must come in through the south gate like everyone else's. Only the car park closes, not the units.

passages.label: Questions 166-169 refer to the following job posting.
passages.content:
MAINTENANCE ENGINEER (NIGHT SHIFT)
Solvarn Components — Ostrava plant

Solvarn Components moulds and finishes technical plastics for the appliance industry. Our Ostrava plant runs continuously, and we are recruiting a maintenance engineer for the night shift.

The role
You will keep sixteen injection-moulding machines and their ancillary equipment running between 10:00 P.M. and 6:00 A.M., four nights on and four nights off. Roughly two thirds of the work is planned maintenance; the rest is breakdown response.

Essential
- A recognised qualification in mechanical or electrical engineering
- At least three years in a manufacturing environment, ideally with hydraulic systems
- Willingness to be first responder to alarms during your shift

Desirable
- Experience of tool changes on machines above 300 tonnes
- Confidence reading engineering drawings in English

What we offer
Salary from $61,000, reviewed after six months. Night allowance of 18%. Four weeks of paid training at our Gdansk plant before you join the line in Ostrava. The company funds one professional course a year.

Send a CV to careers@solvarn.example. We do not accept applications submitted through agencies.

questions.text: What is indicated about the working pattern?
choices: It includes daytime hours at weekends.
It is shared between two engineers.
It alternates blocks of four nights with time off.
questions.explanation: “four nights on and four nights off” describes the rota. The six-month point in the posting is the salary review, not a change of hours.

questions.text: What is an essential requirement of the position?
choices: Fluency in more than one language
Three years of work in manufacturing
questions.explanation: The essential list asks for “at least three years in a manufacturing environment”. Large-tool experience appears under Desirable, and only reading drawings in English is mentioned, not fluency in several languages.

questions.text: What will the successful candidate do before starting work in Ostrava?
choices: Take part in a six-month review
questions.explanation: “Four weeks of paid training at our Gdansk plant before you join the line in Ostrava.” The funded course is an annual benefit once employed.

questions.text: Why does the posting mention agencies?
choices: To identify who will conduct the interviews
To make clear that candidates should apply directly
To explain a delay in filling the position
To indicate that a recruitment fee is payable
questions.explanation: The sentence follows the instruction to send a CV to the company address, so ruling out agency submissions tells applicants to come straight to Solvarn. Refusing such applications also rules out any fee rather than announcing one.

passages.label: Questions 170-171 refer to the following information.
passages.content:
CANDIDATE INFORMATION — Certified Lifting Supervisor (Level 2)
Halberd Training Centre

Assessment takes place on the final afternoon of the course and has three parts.

Written paper (45 minutes). Forty multiple-choice items on load calculation, sling selection and exclusion zones. The pass mark is 30.

Practical observation (about 90 minutes per candidate). You will plan and direct two lifts using the yard gantry. An assessor records whether each step of the plan is briefed to the team before the lift begins.

Oral review (15 minutes). The assessor discusses your decisions with you. This part carries no marks, but a candidate who cannot account for a choice made during the practical may be asked to repeat that lift.

Results are issued within ten working days. A candidate who fails one part only may re-sit that part once, free of charge, within six months. A candidate who fails two or more parts must repeat the whole course at the standard fee.

Bring photographic identification and your own safety footwear. All other equipment is provided.

questions.text: What is stated about the oral review?
choices: It takes place before the practical.
It carries fewer marks than the other parts.
It does not count towards the result.
questions.explanation: “This part carries no marks” — it can only send a candidate back to repeat a lift. The 90 minutes belongs to the practical observation.

questions.text: What is suggested about a candidate who fails both the written paper and the practical observation?
choices: The result will be issued sooner than usual.
Only the written paper has to be taken again.
A further payment will be necessary.
A wait of six months is required.
questions.explanation: Failing two parts means repeating the whole course “at the standard fee”; the free re-sit is reserved for a candidate who fails one part only.

passages.label: Questions 172-175 refer to the following web page.
passages.content:
https://www.calderhouse-lettings.example/landlords

questions.text: What does Managed Plus include that Managed does not?

questions.text: According to the web page, when must a landlord give approval?
choices: Before a tenancy agreement is drawn up
Before an inspection is carried out
Before repair work over a certain value is ordered
questions.explanation: The agency instructs contractors itself, “you approve anything above $400”. Advertising, agreements and inspections are all handled by the agency without a separate approval.

questions.text: What does a landlord receive after a property inspection?
choices: A printed copy of the tenancy agreement
A telephone call from the contractor
A message saying the report is ready
A refund of the set-up fee
questions.explanation: The report goes to the online account within two working days and “we send you a text message as soon as a report is ready”. The set-up fee is waived before 30 June, never refunded afterwards.

passages.label: Questions 176-180 refer to the following press release and e-mail.
passages.content:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

11 January — Aalstrup Components announced today that its new plant at the Rivermouth Industrial Park will begin production on 2 March. The 14,000-square-metre facility will manufacture aluminium housings for electric motors, a line currently produced only at the company's plant in Sandvik.

passages.label: Questions 176-180 refer to the following press release and e-mail.
passages.content:
To: press@aalstrup.example
From: p.rezende@rivermouthtech.example
Date: 10 February
Subject: Open house — apprentice group

Dear Ms. Halvorsen,

I coordinate the technical apprenticeship programme at Rivermouth Technical College, two kilometres from your new site. I would like to bring fourteen second-year apprentices to the open house on the 14th. Rivermouth Technical College

questions.text: What is the purpose of the press release?
choices: To announce the opening of a manufacturing site
To report the company's results for the year
To invite suppliers to submit bids
questions.explanation: The headline and first paragraph announce that a new plant at Rivermouth will begin production on 2 March. Hiring is mentioned, but only as a consequence of the opening.

questions.text: What is indicated about the aluminium housings?
choices: They are currently made at only one Aalstrup plant.
They will replace an older product line.
They are produced for a single customer.
They were designed at the Rivermouth site.
questions.explanation: “a line currently produced only at the company's plant in Sandvik”. Nothing says the product replaces anything or that Rivermouth designed it.

questions.text: What is suggested about Mr. Rezende's e-mail?
choices: It was written before the press release appeared.
It was sent to the wrong department.
It arrived after the date set for registration.
It repeats a request he made by telephone.
questions.explanation: The release asks visitors to register by 7 February, and the e-mail is dated 10 February. The open house itself has not yet taken place, so the message is late rather than too early.

questions.text: What position is held by the person Mr. Rezende wants to address his group?
questions.explanation: He asks for fifteen minutes with Ms. Balogun, whom the press release identifies as the plant manager leading the assembly-floor tours.

questions.text: What does Mr. Rezende ask Ms. Halvorsen to confirm?
choices: The address of the Rivermouth site
The maximum size of a tour group
Whether the open house will be repeated
Whether his apprentices may apply in April
questions.explanation: His second request concerns the April round of hiring and whether it is open to candidates finishing his programme in June.

passages.label: Questions 181-185 refer to the following advertisement and customer review.
passages.content:

Reviewer: Danuta Wrzesniewski, quality supervisor
Rating: 4 out of 5

My employer sent four of us on the course together, which brought the cost of each place down usefully. The instructor, Kwabena Osei, has run a testing laboratory for twenty years, and every rule he taught came with a story about the day somebody ignored it. I passed the examination in November.
